q: בת 92, מאושפזת במחלקת אורתופדיה לאחר ניתוח תיקון שבר צוואר ירך. ברקע: דמנציה, מטופלת ב- DONEPEZIL. במהלך הבתר ניתוחי הצוות שמו לב שהיא ישנונית, אינה מתמצאת בזמן או במקום, מתקשה לבצע הוראות של צוות פיזיותרפיה. יש תנודות במצב ההכרה ובמצב הקוגניטיבי במהלך היום. ביום השני לאחר הניתוח – הוצא צנתר משלפוחית השתן. מעקב שארית שתן- ללא שארית. עקב ניסיון לתלוש את העירוי, ידיה של המטופלת נקשרו. אילו מבין הגורמים הבאים תורם לתסמונת ממנה היא סובלת כעת?
o: פיזיותרפיה בעיתוי מוקדם מדי לאחר הניתוח
הוצאת הצנתר מכיס השתן
קשירה של הידיים
תגובה ממושכת לתרופות אינדוקציה סביב הניתוח
explanation:
The acute cognitive change and fluctuating alertness fit **delirium**, in a postoperative patient with pre-existing dementia. Nonpharmacological care includes early mobility, avoiding restraints, removing unnecessary catheters, protecting sleep and correcting sensory impairments (Hazzard 8e, pp. 883, 888–889).

**A. Physiotherapy too early after surgery.** Wrong, early mobilization is recommended for delirium prevention; the stem does not establish that therapy started too early (p. 888).
**B. Removal of the urinary catheter.** Wrong, minimizing mobility-limiting equipment, including urinary catheters, is part of prevention; the stem also reports no residual urine (p. 888).
**C. Restraining the hands.** Correct, restraints reduce mobility and can increase agitation, injury risk and worsening delirium. This is a documented aggravating factor added during this admission, and the source recommends avoiding it where possible (p. 888).
**D. A prolonged response to perioperative induction drugs.** Wrong, restraints are the explicitly supported aggravating factor among these choices. Anesthetic medications merit review, but a prolonged induction-drug response is not established by the description. This does not claim that anesthesia cannot contribute (pp. 888–889).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 883, 888–889.

q: בן 78, ימני, התקבל למחלקת שיקום גריאטרי לאחר שבץ בטריטוריה של Rt. Middle cerebral artery. מה הממצאים הצפויים פרט לפלגיה משמאל?
o: aphasia
סטיית מבט לשמאל
neglect
חרשות באוזן ימין
explanation:
A **right middle cerebral artery stroke** causes characteristic neurological deficits according to the regions affected (Hazzard 8e, p. 958).

**A. Aphasia.** Wrong, aphasia characterizes injury to the language-dominant hemisphere; in this right-handed patient, neglect is the expected match for the right-sided lesion (p. 958).
**B. Leftward gaze deviation.** Wrong, gaze deviates toward the ischemic hemisphere in a complete MCA syndrome, so rightward deviation is expected here (p. 958).
**C. Neglect.** Correct, nondominant hemispheric injury causes visuospatial and tactile neglect; the source describes left-sided neglect in this syndrome (p. 958).
**D. Deafness in the right ear.** Wrong, impaired auditory language comprehension can accompany injury to language areas, but isolated right-ear deafness is not the MCA syndrome described in the source (p. 958).

Source: Hazzard 8e, p. 958.

q: בת 75, ברקע אי ספיקת לב, סוכרת, יתר לחץ דם, וזיהומים חוזרים בדרכי השתן עם טיפול אנטיביוטי מניעתי. פונה למרפאה בגין קשיי נשימה שהתחילו בצורה הדרגתית. בבדיקתה – סטורציה נמוכה, בהאזנה לריאות – קרפיטציות עדינות דו צדדיות בסוף אינספיריום. לאיזה מהתרופות שמקבלת יכול להיות קשר למחלתה?
o: AMLODIPINE
METFORMIN
SPIRONOLACTONE
NITOFURANTOIN
explanation:
**Official answer: ד — Nitrofurantoin.** Prolonged use is associated with pulmonary toxicity (Hazzard 8e, p. 1708).

**A. Amlodipine.** Wrong, this is not the drug identified by the source as long-term urinary prophylaxis with pulmonary toxicity; the exposure and symptoms point to nitrofurantoin (p. 1708).
**B. Metformin.** Wrong, it does not match the decisive exposure of prolonged antibiotic prophylaxis. This should not be read as a claim that the book excludes every possible pulmonary reaction to metformin (p. 1708).
**C. Spironolactone.** Wrong, underlying heart failure warrants considering other causes of dyspnea, but the explicit drug warning concerning urinary prophylaxis is for nitrofurantoin (p. 1708).
**D. Nitrofurantoin.** Correct, officially accepted; the book emphasizes pulmonary toxicity particularly with long-term use, linking the described exposure to the symptoms (p. 1708).

Source: Hazzard 8e, p. 1708.

q: בת 60, סובלת בחודשים האחרונים משינויים קוגניטיביים ושינויים התנהגותיים. מדברת באופן בוטה, לא מתעניינת בדברים שעינינו אותה בעבר, חוזרת פעמים רבות על אותם משפטים. בבדיקה הקוגניטיבית בולטת פגיעה בתפקודים הניהוליים (Executive functions) והזיכרון יחסית שמור. מה הממצא ההדמייתי האופייני במצב זה?
o: MRI מוח יראה ירידה בנפח המוח
CT אנגיוגרפיה יראה אוטמים מרובים ופגיעה ווסקולרית
מיפוי PET FDG יראה ירידה במטבוליזם באונות הפרונטליות
CT יראה נפח חדרים מוגבר עם השטחה של הסולקים
explanation:
The behavioral changes, impaired executive function, and relatively preserved memory fit **behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD)**. Regional frontal abnormalities are more informative here than nonspecific loss of brain volume (Hazzard 8e, p. 989; application to the vignette).

**A. Brain MRI will show reduced brain volume.** Wrong, volume loss can occur, but this wording omits the frontal and anterior temporal distribution characteristic of the disease. It is less specific than the regional metabolic finding (p. 989).
**B. CT angiography will show multiple infarcts and vascular damage.** Wrong, infarcts and vascular injury are not the characteristic findings described for this behavioral syndrome; the source describes frontal atrophy and metabolic abnormalities (p. 989).
**C. FDG-PET will show reduced metabolism in the frontal lobes.** Correct, bilateral frontal hypometabolism on FDG-PET is described in FTD and fits the behavioral syndrome in this vignette (p. 989).
**D. CT will show enlarged ventricles with effacement of the sulci.** Wrong, this is not the regional neurodegenerative pattern described for FTD and does not fit this presentation as well as the frontal metabolic finding (p. 989; application to the vignette).

In bvFTD, FDG-PET may show bilateral frontal hypometabolism, while structural imaging may show frontal and anterior temporal atrophy. Thus, the regional FDG-PET finding is the characteristic choice among those offered (Hazzard 8e, p. 989).

Source: Hazzard 8e, p. 989.

q: אילו מבין השינויים הבאים של ההזדקנות קשורים להתמודדות אדם זקן עם COPD?
o: עליה ב- cardiac output
ירידה ב- peripheral vascular resistance
ירידה בלחץ בעורקי הריאה
סיכון מוגבר לאוסטאופורוזיס
explanation:
**Osteoporosis** is an important COPD comorbidity, and musculoskeletal impairment adds to age-related functional decline. Systemic inflammation, deconditioning, and other factors contribute; a single unproven mechanism should not be assigned to every patient (pp. 1241–1242).

**A. Increased cardiac output.** Wrong, aging is not described as increasing cardiac output: peak-exercise output declines, and the aging–COPD table describes further reduction with COPD (pp. 1121, 1242).
**B. Decreased peripheral vascular resistance.** Wrong, age-related arterial stiffness accompanies increased peripheral resistance, not the proposed decrease (p. 1242, Table 81-3).
**C. Decreased pulmonary artery pressure.** Wrong, pulmonary vascular loss and hypoxic vasoconstriction in COPD may increase pulmonary pressure; a decrease is not the described effect (p. 1241).
**D. Increased osteoporosis risk.** Correct, age-related bone loss adds to osteoporosis among COPD comorbidities, impairing musculoskeletal capacity and mobility (pp. 1241–1242).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 1121, 1241–1242.

q: בת 70, מתלוננת כי מספר שנים סובלת מרעד בשתי הידיים ובראש אשר החמיר לאחרונה. אינה מסוגלת להשתמש בכף כדי לאכול מרק, כיוון הנוזל נשפך מהכף. שתיית אלכוהול מקלה על הרעד ואילו מתח נפשי מחמיר אותו. בבדיקה מדובר ברעד דו צדדי (יד ימין ויד שמאל) סימטרי בחומרתו, רעד בראש ושאר הבדיקה הנוירולוגית תקינה. מה הטיפול המומלץ לרעד?
o: LEVODOPA+CARBIDOPA (DOPICAR)
Beta blockers
Calcium channel blockers
AMANTADINE
explanation:
The presentation fits **essential tremor**: action or postural tremor, head involvement, and improvement after alcohol are described in the book (Hazzard 8e, pp. 146, 940). For limb tremor, the AAN guideline identifies propranolol among the best-supported treatments.
"Propranolol, propranolol long-acting, or primidone should be offered" (AAN clinician summary, p. 1).

**A. Levodopa plus carbidopa (Dopicar).** Wrong, this treats parkinsonism; the presentation fits essential tremor without the other parkinsonian signs and does not point to that treatment pathway (Hazzard 8e, pp. 940, 944–946).
**B. Beta blockers.** Correct, propranolol is a beta blocker that the guideline recommends offering for limb tremor, taking comorbidities and adverse effects into account. This does not mean that all beta blockers are equivalent (AAN, p. 1).
**C. Calcium channel blockers.** Wrong, this is not a first-line recommendation for the class. The guideline distinguishes nimodipine, which may be considered with limited evidence, from nifedipine and verapamil, which are not recommended for limb tremor (AAN, p. 1).
**D. Amantadine.** Wrong, evidence is insufficient to recommend it for essential tremor; it does not have the same support as propranolol in this case (AAN, p. 1).

**Official answer:** Beta blockers (IMA, final answer key, December 2021, question 92).

The book describes essential tremor during movement or maintained posture, sometimes involving the head and improving after a little alcohol. The bilateral tremor, difficulty using a spoon, head involvement, and alcohol response in the question therefore fit essential tremor. The located source does not provide a treatment rule using beta blockers (Hazzard 8e, pp. 146, 940).

The retained note describes the limitation of the cited Hazzard passages; the treatment recommendation was added from the external guideline that was read (AAN, pp. 1–2).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 146, 940, 944–946; American Academy of Neurology. Evidence-based guideline update: Treatment of essential tremor, clinician summary, 2011, pp. 1–2. https://www.aan.com/Guidelines/home/GetGuidelineContent/493.
explanationReviewNote: The source supports identifying essential tremor from this presentation; reaching beta-blocker treatment also requires an essential-tremor treatment recommendation, which it does not state.

q: בת 84, עצמאית בתפקודה וללא ירידה קוגניטיבית ידועה. ברקע סוכרת ויתר לחץ דם. מה צריך לכלול הטיפול בסוכרת על פי המאמר Older Adults: Standards of Medical Care in Diabetes 2020?
o: איזון סוכרת עם המוגלובין A1C מתחת ל- 7.5% והערכה קוגניטיבית אחת לשנה
איזון סוכרת עם המוגלובין A1C מתחת ל-7% ואיזון לחץ דם מתחת ל- 130/80
איזון סוכרת עם ערכי גלוקוז בצום 100-200 ומתן טיפול בסטטינים
איזון סוכרת עם ערכי גלוקוז בצום 70-100 ובדיקת גילוי מוקדם לכף רגל סוכרתית
explanation:
Official answer: A1C below 7.5% and annual cognitive assessment.

**Treatment targets depend on function and cognition**, not age alone. For the independent patient with preserved cognition, the 2020 framework supports A1C below 7.5% and periodic cognitive screening. Cognitive impairment matters because it complicates glucose monitoring and medication adjustment (ADA 2020, pp. S153–S155).

"for adults 65 years of age or older at the initial visit and annually as appropriate." (ADA 2020, p. S153, Recommendation 12.3.)

**A. A1C below 7.5% and annual cognitive assessment.** Correct, both components are supported: the target fits the relatively healthy group, and Recommendation 12.3 calls for screening at the initial visit and annually as appropriate (Table 12.1; p. S153).
**B. A1C below 7% and blood pressure below 130/80.** Wrong, these are tighter than the stated framework, whose blood-pressure goal is below 140/90. A lower individual glycemic goal can be considered if achieved without recurrent or severe hypoglycemia or undue burden, but is not required for every patient like this (Table 12.1, p. S155).
**C. Fasting glucose 100–200 and a statin.** Wrong, a statin may be appropriate, but the proposed fasting range does not match this group’s 90–130 mg/dL target (Table 12.1, p. S155).
**D. Fasting glucose 70–100 and diabetic-foot screening.** Wrong, complication screening matters, but the proposed fasting range is below the recommendation for this group. Avoid hypoglycemia rather than choosing a tight target solely because diabetes is present (pp. S153–S155).

Source-to-key explanation: In older adults with preserved function and cognition and few comorbid illnesses, Table 12.1 gives A1C below 7.5%. Recommendation 12.3 specifies cognitive screening from age 65 at the initial visit and annually as appropriate, supporting both components of the official answer.

Read from the paper: ADA 2020, Table 12.1; Neurocognitive Function, Recommendation 12.3. [Article](https://diabetesjournals.org/care/article/43/Supplement_1/S152/30489/12-Older-Adults-Standards-of-Medical-Care-in).

Source: American Diabetes Association. 12. Older Adults: Standards of Medical Care in Diabetes—2020. Diabetes Care. 2020;43(Suppl 1):S152–S162, pp. S153–S155, Table 12.1 and Recommendation 12.3, doi:10.2337/dc20-S012.
ref: Standards of Medical Care in Diabetes—2020

q: בת 96, סובלת מדמנציה. גרה בבית עם מטפלת 24 שעות. החולה הולכת עם הליכון בהשגחה. לפני שנתיים חוותה שבץ מוחי ומאז סובלת מחולשת פלג גוף ימין קלה. החולה נפלה שלוש פעמים בשנה החולפת. בבדיקה גופנית לחץ הדם בשכיבה הוא 145/80 ממ"כ, ולאחר שלוש דקות עמידה הוא 110/65 ממ"כ. לחולה מספר גורמי סיכון לנפילות. לאיזה גורם סיכון הקשר החלש ביותר לנפילות?
o: גיל מבוגר
אורתוסטטיזם
שבץ בעבר
ירידה קוגניטיבית
explanation:
Official answer: ב

Table 43-1 ranks the **strength of evidence** associating factors with falls. Orthostatic hypotension has weak evidence, whereas advanced age, stroke and dementia have strong evidence; this does not quantify the individual patient’s risk (p. 635).
"weak evidence (occasionally but not usually found)" (Table 43-1 footnote, p. 635).

**A. Advanced age.** Wrong, the table assigns strong, consistent evidence, rather than the weakest category among these factors (p. 635).
**B. Orthostatic hypotension.** Correct, it has the weakest evidence category among these four. This does not make the measured blood-pressure fall clinically unimportant in this patient (p. 635).
**C. Previous stroke.** Wrong, stroke has strong evidence, unlike orthostatic hypotension (p. 635).
**D. Cognitive impairment.** Wrong, dementia and impaired cognition have strong evidence, so they are not the weakest category requested (p. 635).

Orthostatic hypotension is the official answer to the wording “weakest association.” Read this as strength and consistency of evidence, not a comparative risk ratio.
Source versus explanation: "Strong evidence (consistently found in high-quality studies)" (Table 43-1 footnote, p. 635).
Note: The question does not specify whether “weakest” means consistency of evidence or effect size. The table supports the former interpretation.

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 635.

q: בת 85, הסובלת מסרטן גרורתי ודמנציה מתקדמת הוכרזה כחולה נוטה למות שאינה כשירה. בברור רצונה נמצא כי תוקף ייפוי הכוח עליו חתמה ובו מינתה את שכנתה, פג לפני שנתיים, אך לאחרונה מונה לה אפוטרופוס מטעם המדינה. מי צריך להיות מקבל ההחלטה בעניין הטיפול בסוף החיים?
o: האפוטרופוס
אחייניתה שהינה קרובת המשפחה היחידה שלה
הרופא האחראי בהתייעצות עם השכנה
הרופא האחראי בהתייעצות עם האפוטרופוס
explanation:
**התשובה הרשמית:** הרופא האחראי בהתייעצות עם השכנה (הר״י IMA, מפתח התשובות הסופי, מועד 2021-Dec, שאלה 95).

סעיף 39(ב) קובע שייפוי כוח שפג תוקפו אינו מחייב, אך הרופא האחראי חייב לעיין בו ורשאי להתחשב בו. זה חל על ייפוי הכוח לשכנה שפג בשאלה. סעיפים 5(ג) ו־29 מבחינים גם במעמד אדם קרוב ואפוטרופוס ובבירור רצון החולה; הנתונים אינם משלימים את התנאים להעדפת התייעצות עם השכנה דווקא (חוק החולה הנוטה למות, סעיפים 5(ג), 29, 39(ב), PDF עמ׳ 6, 15, 19).

**א. האפוטרופוס.** שגויה, מינוי אפוטרופוס אינו הופך אותו לבדו למכריע בטיפול לפי חוק זה. סעיף 29 מתאר החלטות בשילוב הרופא האחראי ולעיתים הכרעת ועדה מוסדית (עמ׳ PDF 15).
**ב. אחייניתה שהינה קרובת המשפחה היחידה שלה.** שגויה, קרבת משפחה אינה לבדה סמכות הכרעה; סעיף 5(ג) עוסק בהצהרת אדם קרוב על רצון החולה במסגרת החלטת הרופא האחראי (עמ׳ PDF 6).
**ג. הרופא האחראי בהתייעצות עם השכנה.** נכונה, נכונה לניקוד הרשמי. ייפוי הכוח שפג אינו מחייב, אך הרופא חייב לעיין בו ורשאי להתחשב בו; העמוד תומך בהתחשבות במסמך, ולא משלים את הנתון החסר על מעמד השכנה לצורך העדפתה (סעיפים 5(ג), 39(ב), עמ׳ PDF 6 ו־19).
**ד. הרופא האחראי בהתייעצות עם האפוטרופוס.** שגויה, אינה התשובה שהתקבלה במפתח. מעמד האפוטרופוס תלוי בתנאים שבסעיפים 5(ג) ו־29, ולכן אין להפוך את הפסילה בבחינה לכלל שלפיו אין להתייעץ עם אפוטרופוס (עמ׳ PDF 6 ו־15).

מקור: חוק החולה הנוטה למות, סעיפים 5(ג), 29, 39(ב), עמ׳ PDF 6, 15, 19.
ref: חוק החולה הנוטה למות; section not specified

q: מה הייחוד של טיפול פליאטיבי בחולי דמנציה מטיפול פליאטיבי בחולים אונקולוגים?
o: בחולי דמנציה אין צורך בטיפול בכאב היות והשכיחות של כאב היא נמוכה
טיפול פליאטיבי בחולי דמנציה יכול התבצע בצורה טובה על ידי הצוות המטפל ואין חשיבות להכנסה של מומחים בטיפול פליאטיבי
חולי דמנציה מתקדמת סובלים מנטל סימפטומים גופניים משמעותי ובזה אינם שונים מחולים אונקולוגים
שילוב של טיפול פליאטיבי בחולי דמנציה חשוב רק בשלבים המתקדמים של המחלה
explanation:
Hazzard describes increasing **symptom burden in advanced dementia**, including pain, dysphagia, weight loss, and infections needing palliation (pp. 1047–1048). It also describes a high symptom burden in cancer (p. 1071). The inference supporting the official answer is that both populations have substantial physical symptoms, not that every symptom has identical frequency or severity.

**A. Patients with dementia do not need pain treatment because pain is uncommon.** Wrong, the source describes pain and the need to assess and relieve it in advanced dementia; inability to report it does not remove the need for treatment (p. 1048).
**B. The usual team can provide palliative care well, and specialist involvement is unimportant.** Wrong, primary palliative care belongs within usual care, but the source also includes referral to specialist teams when needed; dismissing their importance is unjustified (p. 1045).
**C. Advanced dementia has a substantial physical symptom burden, as does cancer.** Correct, officially accepted. The comparison concerns the existence of substantial burden, as explained in the source-based inference, not identity of every symptom (pp. 1047–1048, 1071).
**D. Palliative care matters only in advanced dementia.** Wrong, palliative care is appropriate at any stage of serious illness and can accompany disease treatment; it need not wait until advanced dementia (p. 1045).

**Official answer:** Patients with advanced dementia have a substantial physical symptom burden and in this respect do not differ from patients with cancer (IMA final answer key, December 2021, question 96).

The source-based comparison is an inference: significant physical symptom burden occurs in both groups; it does not establish identical symptom frequencies or intensities (Hazzard 8e, pp. 1047–1048, 1071).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 1045, 1047–1048, 1071.

q: הוזמן ייעוץ שיקומי לבן 79 המאושפז במחלקה כירורגית לאחר כריתת כיס מרה דחופה. החולה מוזן כעת בזונדה, משתף פעולה חלקית בפיזיותרפיה ובבדיקה נמצא פצע לחץ דרגה 3 בעכוז. במעבדה- לויקוציטים 11,400, CRP-13. מה ההמלצה להמשך שיקום לחולה זה?
o: בשל פצע לחץ דרגה 3 מתאים למחלקה לסיעוד מורכב בלבד
לצורך קבלתו למחלקת שיקום יש לגמול אותו קודם מזונדה
יש להמתין עד להתנרמלות מדדי דלקת ואז לקבלו לשיקום
ניתן לקבלו למחלקה שיקומית בתנאי שמסכים ומשתף פעולה בטיפול
explanation:
**התשובה הרשמית:** יש להמתין עד להתנרמלות מדדי דלקת ואז לקבלו לשיקום; ניתן לקבלו למחלקה שיקומית בתנאי שמסכים ומשתף פעולה בטיפול (הר״י IMA, מפתח התשובות הסופי, מועד 2021-Dec, שאלה 97).

החוזר קובע שפצע לחץ או זונדה שאינם מונעים טיפול שיקומי אינם התוויית נגד לשיקום, ושנדרשים יכולת לימוד ושיתוף פעולה לצד יציבות רפואית. בשאלה מופיעים זונדה, פצע לחץ ושיתוף פעולה חלקי; לכן עצם קיומם אינו שולל קבלה, וניתן להסיק את האפשרות המותנית בהסכמה ובשיתוף פעולה לאחר הערכת היציבות. החוזר אינו דורש שמדדי הדלקת יתנרמלו (חוזר משרד הבריאות 4/2009, סעיפים 5.2–5.3, PDF עמ׳ 4).

**א. פצע לחץ דרגה 3 מחייב סיעוד מורכב בלבד.** שגויה, פצע שאינו מונע טיפול שיקומי אינו התוויית נגד לשיקום; יש להעריך את השפעתו בפועל (סעיף 5.3(א), PDF עמ׳ 4).
**ב. יש לגמול מזונדה לפני שיקום.** שגויה, הזנה בזונדה שאינה מונעת טיפול אינה עילה לדחיית שיקום (סעיף 5.3(ג), PDF עמ׳ 4).
**ג. להמתין להתנרמלות מדדי הדלקת.** נכונה לצורכי ניקוד לפי הקבלה הרשמית. מבחינה קלינית, הסעיף דורש הערכת מצב ויציבות רפואית; הוא אינו דורש כשלעצמו נרמול של מדדי מעבדה (סעיף 5.2(א), PDF עמ׳ 4).
**ד. קבלה בהסכמה ובשיתוף פעולה.** נכונה לצורכי ניקוד וגם נתמכת בתנאי שיתוף הפעולה וההסכמה, בצירוף הערכת היציבות הרפואית (סעיפים 5.2, 5.4, PDF עמ׳ 4).

מקור: חוזר משרד הבריאות 4/2009, סעיפים 5.2–5.4, PDF עמ׳ 4.
ref: משרד הבריאות — אמות מידה למתן טיפול שיקומי לקשישים

q: בת 88 פנתה למיון עקב שקיעה במצב ההכרה. לפני שבוע נפלה ונחבלה וסבלה מכאבים קשים. המשפחה יודעת שהחולה לקחה תכשירים שונים לשיכוך כאב, ולאחר מכן הפכה להיות שקועה. המשפחה מביאה שקית עם תרופות אנלגטיות שונות אותן החולה לקחה בבית בשבוע האחרון. מי מבין התרופות האנלגטיות הבאות יכולה לגרום בסבירות גבוהה לשקיעה הכרתית?
o: ACAMOL FOCUS (PARACETAMOL, ASPIRIN, CAFFEINE)
COMBODEX (PARACETAMOL, IBUPROFEN)
MUSCOL (PARACETAMOL, ORPHENADRINE)
DIPYRONE (OPTALGIN)
explanation:
**Orphenadrine** is a skeletal muscle relaxant with anticholinergic effects and a risk of sedation in older adults. The Beers Criteria classify it as potentially inappropriate and recommend avoidance, supporting MUSCOL as the answer in this comparison (Beers 2023, pp. 2063, 2074).

**A. ACAMOL FOCUS (paracetamol, aspirin, caffeine).** Wrong, the listed formulation contains no orphenadrine. The supported explanation for sedation here is MUSCOL's anticholinergic muscle relaxant, rather than analgesic use itself (p. 2063).
**B. COMBODEX (paracetamol, ibuprofen).** Wrong, the table's main warnings for ibuprofen concern bleeding and kidney injury; orphenadrine is the component explaining sedation in this comparison (p. 2063).
**C. MUSCOL (paracetamol, orphenadrine).** Correct, it contains orphenadrine, explicitly listed among muscle relaxants poorly tolerated because of sedation and anticholinergic effects (pp. 2063, 2074).
**D. DIPYRONE (OPTALGIN).** Wrong, dipyrone is not the anticholinergic component identified here. This distinguishes the formulations in the question without claiming that other analgesics have no risks (pp. 2063, 2074).

Source: AGS Beers Criteria 2023, pp. 2063, 2074 (PDF pp. 12, 23).

q: מה מאפיין את הזקנים בארץ מבחינה פסיכו-סוציאלית לפי לקט הנתונים האינפוגרפי של השנתון הסטטיסטי?
o: אחוז בני 65+ בקרב הרוגים ופצועים קשה בתאונות דרכים גדול מחלקם באוכלוסייה
קופת חולים מכבי היא בעלת אחוז הזקנים הגבוה ביותר
כ- 8% מבני 75 ומעלה שוהים במוסד
רוב הנשים בנות 70 ומעלה מקבלות "גמלת סיעוד"
explanation:
יש להשוות **אותה אוכלוסייה ואותו מכנה**: חלקם של מבוגרים בכלל האוכלוסייה מול חלקם בנפגעי תאונות קשות, ושיעור מקבלות גמלת סיעוד מתוך כלל הנשים בקבוצת הגיל. כאן הבדיקה נשענת על שנתון 2024 שברשימת הקריאה; אין זו בדיקה ישירה של המהדורה ההיסטורית שנבחנה (עמ׳ 34, 36–37, 41–42, 63).

**א. אחוז בני 65+ בקרב הרוגים ופצועים קשה בתאונות דרכים גדול מחלקם באוכלוסייה.** נכונה, האינפוגרפיקה קובעת במפורש כי חלקם של בני 65 ומעלה בהרוגים ובפצועים קשה גדול מחלקם באוכלוסייה; זהו ייצוג־יתר, בלי צורך להמציא סיבות שלא נבדקו בעמוד (עמ׳ 36).
**ב. קופת חולים מכבי היא בעלת אחוז הזקנים הגבוה ביותר.** שגויה, בתרשים שיעור המבוגרים מבין מבוטחי כל קופה גבוה יותר בכללית מאשר במכבי; יש להבחין בין שיעור בתוך קופה לבין חלוקת כלל המבוגרים בין הקופות (עמ׳ 37).
**ג. כ- 8% מבני 75 ומעלה שוהים במוסד.** שגויה, שיעור השוהים במוסד בשתי קבוצות הגיל המרכיבות את בני 75 ומעלה נמוך מן השיעור שבאפשרות; גם ממוצע משוקלל שלהן אינו מגיע אליו (עמ׳ 42).
**ד. רוב הנשים בנות 70 ומעלה מקבלות "גמלת סיעוד".** שגויה, השיעור עולה עם הגיל, אך אין להחיל את שיעור הקבוצה המבוגרת ביותר על כל הנשים בנות 70 ומעלה. כהסקה חישובית, שקלול השיעורים לפי קבוצות הגיל בתרשים באמצעות מבנה אוכלוסיית הנשים אינו מצביע על רוב; החישוב משתמש בנתונים מעוגלים ולכן אינו מוצג כשיעור מדויק (עמ׳ 41, 63).

א׳ נתמכת במהדורה המקומית המאוחרת: בני 65 ומעלה מהווים 21% מההרוגים ו־19% מהפצועים קשה בתאונות דרכים, ושיעורם בקבוצות אלה גדול מחלקם באוכלוסייה. זהו אימות לפי שנתון 2024, ולא אימות המספרים בשנתון ההיסטורי שנבחן (בני 65+ בישראל, שנתון 2024, עמ׳ מודפס 36).

אפשרות ב שגויה: בשנתון 2024, עמ׳ מודפס 37, שיעור בני 65+ מכלל מבוטחי הקופה גבוה ביותר בכללית (14%), לעומת מכבי (13%); אלו נתוני מהדורת 2024, ולא אימות של המספרים במהדורת הבחינה הישנה.

מקור: שנור י, דוידוביץ נ (עורכים). בני 65+ בישראל, שנתון סטטיסטי 2024, מס׳ 26. מכון מאיירס־ג׳וינט־ברוקדייל, עמ׳ 34, 36–37, 41–42, 63 (לוח 1.2).
referenceNote: Brookdale yearbook: לקט נתונים אינפוגרפי. Examined on an earlier edition; figures may differ from the required 2024 edition.

q: בת 75, אושפזה בשל חשד לדלקת ריאות במחלקה הפנימית, בשל שיעול של כשבועיים. במהלך אשפוזה בוצע CT ריאות, ללא לתסנין, אולם הודגמו ממצאים בבלוטת התריס. תפקודי תריס נלקחו, אשר תקינים. באיזה ממצא בתירואיד יש להמשיך בברור על ידי FNA?
o: יש לדגום כל Multinodular Goiter (MNG) בשל סיכון לממאירות
נודול סולידי (Solid) בגודל של 2 ס"מ, עם מיקרוקלציפיקציות
יש לדגום כל נודול ציסטי (Purely cystic nodules), לשלילת Cystic Carcinoma
גוש "חם" במיפוי תירואיד
explanation:
An incidental **thyroid nodule** does not automatically require biopsy. The decision depends on size, ultrasound characteristics and function (Hazzard 8e, p. 1555).

**A. Sample every multinodular goiter because of malignancy risk.** Wrong, sample nodules meeting aspiration criteria; multinodularity alone does not require sampling all nodules (p. 1555).
**B. A 2-cm solid nodule with microcalcifications.** Correct, its size and solid composition meet sampling criteria, and microcalcifications add a suspicious feature. Inference: normal thyroid function does not remove the structural concern (p. 1555).
**C. Sample every purely cystic nodule to exclude cystic carcinoma.** Wrong, the table states that purely cystic nodules do not require FNA; this option gives no suspicious solid component (p. 1555).
**D. A hot nodule on thyroid scintigraphy.** Wrong, functioning hot nodules rarely harbor malignancy and do not require cytologic evaluation according to the source (p. 1555).

Source: Hazzard 8e, p. 1555.

q: A 78-year-old man is hospitalized with pneumonia. On day three, he becomes agitated, pulls at IV lines, and is disoriented after being oriented that morning. In addition to the acute change, which finding is central to delirium assessment?
o: Disorganized thinking
Inattention
Altered level of consciousness
Hallucinations
explanation:
**Inattention** and acute onset are the central features of delirium. Difficulty focusing, maintaining, or shifting attention is distinct from associated thought, consciousness, or perceptual changes (p. 883).
"Acute onset and inattention are the central features of delirium." (p. 883).

**A. Disorganized thinking.** Wrong, Disorganized thought is an additional major feature; it does not replace assessment of attention (p. 883).
**B. Inattention.** Correct, Inattention is the central feature paired with acute onset in the source (p. 883).
**C. Altered level of consciousness.** Wrong, An altered level of consciousness is an additional feature, rather than a substitute for inattention (p. 883).
**D. Hallucinations.** Wrong, Hallucinations are associated perceptual disturbances and are explicitly not cardinal elements (p. 883).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 883.
ref: Hazzard Ch 58 — DELIRIUM · Harrison Ch 433 — Approach to the Patient with Neurologic Disease

q: A 72-year-old woman takes diphenhydramine every night for sleep and reports morning drowsiness. Which explanation is consistent with Hazzard?
o: A short half-life confines the sedating effect to the evening
Tolerance to the sedating effect develops slowly over years
A long half-life contributes to sedation on the following day
Antihistaminergic activity increases alertness after taking the drug
explanation:
**Diphenhydramine** causes sedation through potent antihistaminergic effects, and its long half-life can produce next-day sedation. Tolerance to the sedating effect develops rapidly; this does not make it a suitable primary treatment for insomnia in older adults (p. 661). "The long half-life of diphenhydramine may result in next-day sedation." (p. 661).

**A. A short half-life confines the sedating effect to the evening.** Wrong, the source identifies a long half-life and next-day sedation, so evening-only sedation is not supported (p. 661).
**B. Tolerance to the sedating effect develops slowly over years.** Wrong, the source describes rapid development of tolerance rather than a process taking years (p. 661).
**C. A long half-life contributes to sedation on the following day.** Correct, next-day sedation from the long half-life fits the reported morning drowsiness (p. 661).
**D. Antihistaminergic activity increases alertness after taking the drug.** Wrong, the antihistaminergic effect is described as sedating, not alerting (p. 661).

Source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th ed., pp. 661.
ref: Hazzard Ch 22 — MEDICATION PRESCRIBING AND DE-PRESCRIBING

q: A 68-year-old man is referred for comprehensive geriatric assessment after a recent hospitalization. He is independent in basic activities of daily living but needs help managing medications, paying bills, and shopping. How should his functional status be characterized?
o: Dependent in basic ADLs but independent in IADLs; needs help with self-care
Independent in basic ADLs, dependent in IADLs; needs household assistance
Independent in basic ADLs and IADLs; needs help with recreational activities
Dependent in basic ADLs and IADLs; needs help with feeding and transfers
explanation:
**Basic ADLs** concern self-care, whereas **IADLs** concern maintaining an independent household (p. 123). The latter include shopping, taking medications, and handling finances; needing help with these tasks indicates IADL dependence while the stem explicitly preserves basic self-care independence (p. 123; application to the case). "BADLs refer to self-care tasks such as bathing, dressing, toileting, continence, grooming, feeding, and transferring." (p. 123).

**A. Dependent in basic ADLs but independent in IADLs; needs help with self-care.** Wrong, the deficits described involve household tasks, and the stem states that basic self-care is independent (p. 123; application).
**B. Independent in basic ADLs, dependent in IADLs; needs household assistance.** Correct, medications, finances, and shopping are instrumental tasks, so the distinction matches the reported abilities (p. 123).
**C. Independent in basic ADLs and IADLs; needs help with recreational activities.** Wrong, he already needs help with IADLs; this is not a limitation confined to recreational activities (p. 123).
**D. Dependent in basic ADLs and IADLs; needs help with feeding and transfers.** Wrong, the stem does not describe dependence in feeding or transfers, which are basic ADLs (p. 123).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 123.
ref: Hazzard Ch 8 — PRINCIPLES OF GERIATRIC ASSESSMENT

q: A woman is eating little and losing weight because her sense of taste has changed. Which evaluation appears in the dysgeusia branch of the Hazzard weight-loss algorithm?
o: Assess oral health, medications, and zinc deficiency
Assess thyroid disease, diabetes, and a catabolic condition
Assess food access and the need for meal-delivery assistance
Assess depressive symptoms and the need for counseling
explanation:
The weight-loss algorithm links **dysgeusia** to potentially relevant oral, medication, and nutritional factors. Its dysgeusia branch reads, "Poor oral health, drugs? Zinc deficiency?" (p. 427, Figure 30-8). The other evaluations occupy different branches of the algorithm, so they are not the branch requested here.

**A. Assess oral health, medications, and zinc deficiency.** Correct, these are the factors specifically linked to dysgeusia in the figure (p. 427).
**B. Assess thyroid disease, diabetes, and a catabolic condition.** Wrong, thyroid disease and diabetes appear under altered metabolism or catabolism, not under the taste-disturbance branch (p. 427).
**C. Assess food access and the need for meal-delivery assistance.** Wrong, meal delivery and assistance address inadequate access to food in the figure, not the dysgeusia branch (p. 427).
**D. Assess depressive symptoms and the need for counseling.** Wrong, counseling belongs to the depression branch, whereas the stated question asks for the taste-disturbance evaluation (p. 427).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 427.
ref: Hazzard Ch 49 — MUSCLE AGING AND SARCOPENIA · Harrison Ch 50 — Unintentional Weight Loss

q: A 76-year-old woman with dementia has agitation. In which circumstance should antipsychotic treatment be considered according to the approach in Hazzard?
o: Mild symptoms after environmental interventions have been tried
Severe, dangerous symptoms after a nonpharmacologic treatment trial
Mild symptoms before environmental triggers have been investigated
Stable symptoms to prevent a future behavioral deterioration
explanation:
**Antipsychotic use requires a risk–benefit assessment.** Hazzard describes modest efficacy and important adverse effects, including increased mortality, and reserves use for severe, dangerous symptoms after nonpharmacologic approaches have been tried (p. 927). The guideline emphasizes "reserving antipsychotics for when nonpharmacologic approaches have been tried, and when symptoms are severe and dangerous." (p. 927).

**A. Mild symptoms after environmental interventions have been tried.** Wrong, mild symptoms do not meet the stated severe-and-dangerous symptom criterion (p. 927).
**B. Severe, dangerous symptoms after a nonpharmacologic treatment trial.** Correct, both the prior nonpharmacologic trial and symptom severity match the stated conditions (p. 927).
**C. Mild symptoms before environmental triggers have been investigated.** Wrong, this lacks both the required symptom severity and prior nonpharmacologic approach (p. 927).
**D. Stable symptoms to prevent a future behavioral deterioration.** Wrong, the source reserves treatment for the specified current symptom burden, rather than preventive treatment of stable symptoms (p. 927).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 927.
ref: Hazzard Ch 60 — BEHAVIORAL SYMPTOMS OF DEMENTIA AND PSYCHOACTIVE DRUG THERAPY · Harrison Ch 436 — Seizures and Epilepsy
chapterTitle: Behavioral Symptoms of Dementia and Psychoactive Drug Therapy

q: Which principle describes the weekly high-dose treatment option for severe vitamin D deficiency in Hazzard?
o: Continue high-dose replacement long term instead of changing to maintenance
Use a replacement course followed by a daily maintenance dose
Continue replacement until hypercalciuria appears, then change to maintenance
Start maintenance dosing and increase it when serum calcium rises
explanation:
**Replacement followed by maintenance** is the sequence described for the weekly high-dose option. Hazzard separately identifies hypercalciuria as an early sign of overtreatment, with hypercalcemia occurring subsequently; these are toxicity signals rather than treatment targets. (p. 1540)
"vitamin D2 50,000 IU weekly for 8 to 12 weeks, then vitamin D3 800 to1000 IU daily." (p. 1540)
"The first indication of over-treatment with vitamin D is hypercalciuria which predisposes individuals to nephrolithiasis, and subsequently, hypercalcemia." (p. 1540)

**A. Continue high-dose replacement long term instead of changing to maintenance.** Wrong, the described weekly course is followed by daily vitamin D, rather than continued as the long-term replacement regimen. (p. 1540)
**B. Use a replacement course followed by a daily maintenance dose.** Correct, this preserves the sequence of correcting deficiency and then using a daily maintenance regimen. (p. 1540)
**C. Continue replacement until hypercalciuria appears, then change to maintenance.** Wrong, hypercalciuria is a sign of overtreatment, not the target for ending the replacement course. (p. 1540)
**D. Start maintenance dosing and increase it when serum calcium rises.** Wrong, a rise in calcium is described in the toxicity sequence and is not a reason to escalate treatment. (p. 1540)

Source: Hazzard’s Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th ed., p. 1540.
ref: Hazzard Ch 51 — OSTEOPOROSIS· Harrison Ch 50 — Unintentional Weight Loss

q: In the Fried frailty phenotype, meeting at least three of five criteria identifies frailty. What underlying process does this model propose?
o: Preserved adaptation to stress despite slower performance of daily activities
Reduced risk of losing independence in the absence of an acute precipitating event
Dysregulated stress responses with loss of capacity to maintain homeostasis
Increased physiologic reserve in response to reduced activity and weight loss
explanation:
The **frailty phenotype** is linked to dysregulation of stress-response systems and loss of homeostatic capacity. Its clinical features represent a cycle of declining energy and reserve, and the severity of frailty predicts disability and loss of independence even without an acute precipitant (p. 619).
"frailty is the result of dysregulation of the stress response systems responsible for organismal resilience, leading to loss of homeostatic capabilities, increased susceptibility to stress," (p. 619).
"the severity of frailty is associated with risk for disability and loss of independence, even in the absence of an acute precipitant." (p. 619).

**A. Preserved adaptation to stress despite slower performance of daily activities.** Wrong, preserved stress adaptation conflicts with the model's dysregulated response systems and increased susceptibility to stress (p. 619).
**B. Reduced risk of losing independence in the absence of an acute precipitating event.** Wrong, frailty is associated with disability and loss of independence even without an acute precipitating event, rather than reduced risk in its absence (p. 619).
**C. Dysregulated stress responses with loss of capacity to maintain homeostasis.** Correct, it matches the proposed dysregulation and loss of homeostatic capability underlying the phenotype (p. 619).
**D. Increased physiologic reserve in response to reduced activity and weight loss.** Wrong, reserve declines in the described pathologic cycle; reduced activity and weight loss do not represent an increase in reserve (p. 619).

Source: Hazzard’s Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8e, pp. 619.

q: A 79-year-old woman taking sertraline reports improvement in mood but continues to lose weight unintentionally. What is the appropriate approach to investigating the weight loss?
o: Attribute the loss to the medication and wait for spontaneous change
Assess dietary intake, underlying disease and remediable factors
Attribute the loss to depression and increase the antidepressant dose
Attribute the loss to age and continue monitoring mood alone
explanation:
**Unintentional weight loss** warrants evaluation for underlying and potentially remediable causes. Hazzard recommends verifying weight loss, assessing the adequacy of caloric intake, and directing further testing from the history, examination and basic evaluation (p. 425).
"Initial management of patients with PEM and/or weight loss should include a thorough evaluation to identify underlying causes" (p. 425).
"to aggressively attempt to correct potentially remediable factors." (p. 425).

**A. Attribute the loss to the medication and wait for spontaneous change.** Wrong, assigning the cause to a medication without evaluation bypasses the recommended search for underlying and remediable causes (p. 425).
**B. Assess dietary intake, underlying disease and remediable factors.** Correct, this addresses both intake and possible underlying causes before selecting treatment (p. 425).
**C. Attribute the loss to depression and increase the antidepressant dose.** Wrong, depression is a possible contributor, but the source recommends evaluation rather than assuming it explains persistent weight loss (p. 425).
**D. Attribute the loss to age and continue monitoring mood alone.** Wrong, age alone does not replace the recommended evaluation of involuntary weight loss (p. 425).

Source: Hazzard’s Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8e, pp. 425.
ref: Hazzard Ch 60 — BEHAVIORAL SYMPTOMS OF DEMENTIA AND PSYCHOACTIVE DRUG THERAPY
chapterTitle: Behavioral Symptoms of Dementia and Psychoactive Drug Therapy

q: A 75-year-old man with COPD develops confusion and fatigue over 12 hours. His family says he is unlike his usual self. He is inattentive, lethargic, and less active than usual. Heart rate is 88/min, blood pressure 140/85 mm Hg, respiratory rate 18/min, and oxygen saturation 92% on home oxygen. Which interpretation and initial approach fit this presentation?
o: Chronic dementia; assess gradual cognitive progression at follow-up
Hypoactive delirium; investigate and treat acute contributors
Primary depression; prioritize mood treatment before medical evaluation
Hyperactive delirium; prioritize sedation before precipitant evaluation
explanation:
**Acute inattention** and reduced psychomotor activity support hypoactive delirium. Hazzard describes this form as “characterized by lethargy and reduced psychomotor functioning” (p. 883). Evaluation must identify potentially treatable contributors, including occult illness, rather than treating low activity as ordinary fatigue or chronic decline (pp. 883, 885).

**A. Chronic dementia; assess gradual cognitive progression at follow-up.** Wrong, dementia typically develops insidiously, whereas this change occurred over hours with inattention (pp. 883, 885).
**B. Hypoactive delirium; investigate and treat acute contributors.** Correct, the acute change, inattention, and lethargy fit hypoactive delirium and require evaluation of its causes (pp. 883, 885).
**C. Primary depression; prioritize mood treatment before medical evaluation.** Wrong, low activity in hypoactive delirium can be mistaken for low mood; acute delirium features require medical evaluation (pp. 883, 886).
**D. Hyperactive delirium; prioritize sedation before precipitant evaluation.** Wrong, hyperactive delirium is characterized by agitation and increased vigilance, and medication is not the initial approach to a lethargic patient (pp. 883, 888).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 883, 885, 886.
ref: Hazzard Ch 58 — DELIRIUM · Harrison Ch 433 — Approach to the Patient with Neurologic Disease

q: A woman taking warfarin for atrial fibrillation starts ibuprofen for pain. Which medication approach addresses a modifiable bleeding risk?
o: Continue ibuprofen and rely on INR monitoring to address the risk
Avoid the NSAID and assess another approach to pain relief
Increase ibuprofen to permit a reduction in anticoagulant treatment
Replace ibuprofen with regular aspirin for continuing pain relief
explanation:
**Bleeding-risk reduction** includes addressing interacting medications as well as monitoring anticoagulation (p. 1202). Hazzard specifies "avoidance of NSAIDs and elimination of antiplatelet agents if possible" (p. 1202). Continuing or substituting these exposures does not implement that recommendation.

**A. Continue ibuprofen and rely on INR monitoring to address the risk.** Wrong, Monitoring does not remove the NSAID exposure identified as a modifiable risk (p. 1202).
**B. Avoid the NSAID and assess another approach to pain relief.** Correct, Avoiding the NSAID follows the source's risk-reduction approach (p. 1202).
**C. Increase ibuprofen to permit a reduction in anticoagulant treatment.** Wrong, Increasing NSAID exposure runs against the recommendation to avoid it (p. 1202).
**D. Replace ibuprofen with regular aspirin for continuing pain relief.** Wrong, Substitution with an antiplatelet does not follow the recommendation to eliminate antiplatelet exposure when possible (p. 1202).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 1202.
ref: Hazzard Ch 22 — MEDICATION PRESCRIBING AND DE-PRESCRIBING· Harrison Ch 286 — ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction

q: על פי הנתונים האפידמיולוגיים הנוכחיים, מהי הסיבה המובילה לתמותה במבוגרים מעל גיל 65?
o: infection/sepsis
דמנציה/אלצהיימר
מחלת לב (27%)
פציעות הקשורות ל-falls
explanation:
מחלת לב נותרת הגורם המוביל לתמותה במבוגרים מעל גיל 65, ומהווה כ-27% מהתמותה באוכלוסייה זו על פי נתוני ה-CDC ו-National Vital Statistics. הדבר משקף את הנטל המצטבר של טרשת עורקים, hypertension, heart failure ואריתמיות המואצות עם הגיל. כפי שמודגש ב-Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine, שינויים קרדיווסקולריים הקשורים לגיל — כולל הקשחת העורקים, left ventricular hypertrophy ודיספונקציה אנדותליאלית — יוצרים substrate למחלת לב איסכמית ול-heart failure, מה שהופך את התמותה הקרדיווסקולרית לגורם הדומיננטי בכמעט כל תת-קבוצות המבוגרים.

Infection/sepsis (A) הוא גורם משמעותי לתחלואה ותמותה במבוגרים בשל immunosenescence וקומורבידיות, אך אינו מדורג כגורם המוביל לתמותה. דמנציה/אלצהיימר (B) מדורגים במקום החמישי או השישי בגורמי התמותה בקבוצת גיל זו, וככל הנראה מדווחים בחסר בתעודות הפטירה, אך גם עם תיעוד משופר אינם עולים על מחלת לב. פציעות הקשורות ל-falls (D), למרות שהן syndrome גריאטרי מרכזי הגורם לתחלואה ניכרת, מהוות שיעור קטן בהרבה מהתמותה — פציעות לא-מכוונות (כולל falls) מדורגות בסך הכל נמוך ממחלת לב, סרטן ומחלה צרברווסקולרית.

**Clinical pearl:** שלושת גורמי התמותה המובילים במבוגרים הם מחלת לב, סרטן ומחלה צרברווסקולרית — עובדה הנבחנת לעיתים קרובות. חשוב לזכור שמיתות הקשורות לדמנציה נספרות בחסר מערכתי, מכיוון שדמנציה מושמטת לעיתים קרובות כגורם בסיסי בתעודות הפטירה.
ref: Hazzard Ch 2 — DEMOGRAPHY AND EPIDEMIOLOGY· Harrison Ch 433 — Approach to the Patient with Neurologic Disease

q: A 74-year-old woman with a previous hip fracture takes a long-acting benzodiazepine. Which rationale in Beers 2023 supports reducing exposure?
o: Increased sensitivity and slower metabolism of long-acting agents contribute to harm
Reduced sensitivity with age supports increasing the subsequent medication dose
Switching to a short-acting agent provides a demonstrated reduction in falls risk
Faster metabolism of long-acting agents explains the need for prolonged treatment
explanation:
**Benzodiazepines** pose particular problems in older adults because sensitivity increases and metabolism of long-acting agents decreases. The criteria associate the class with falls and fractures and state that shorter-acting agents are not safer (pp. 2060, 2066).
"Older adults have increased sensitivity to benzodiazepines and decreased metabolism of long-acting agents;" (p. 2060).
"Benzodiazepines: shorter-acting ones are not safer than long-acting ones." (p. 2066).

**A. Increased sensitivity and slower metabolism of long-acting agents contribute to harm.** Correct, This is the age-related sensitivity and metabolism pattern stated by the criteria (p. 2060).
**B. Reduced sensitivity with age supports increasing the subsequent medication dose.** Wrong, The source describes increased sensitivity, which argues against escalating treatment on the assumption of reduced sensitivity (p. 2060).
**C. Switching to a short-acting agent provides a demonstrated reduction in falls risk.** Wrong, The falls section explicitly states that shorter-acting benzodiazepines are not safer than long-acting ones (p. 2066).
**D. Faster metabolism of long-acting agents explains the need for prolonged treatment.** Wrong, The source describes decreased metabolism of long-acting agents, not faster metabolism (p. 2060).

Source: AGS Beers Criteria 2023, pp. 2060, 2066.
ref: Hazzard Ch 22 — MEDICATION PRESCRIBING AND DE-PRESCRIBING

q: Which nutritional approach to sarcopenia is consistent with the evidence described in Hazzard?
o: Consider vitamin D on the basis of demonstrated improvement in muscle function in sarcopenia
Review food intake and consider high-protein supplements when usual food does not meet requirements
Consider isolated leucine on the basis of demonstrated effects independent of complete nutritional supplements
Spread additional protein throughout the day in preference to timing a protein boost near exercise
explanation:
**Nutritional assessment** identifies whether usual food meets protein requirements. Hazzard allows supplementation when it does not: "When the required levels of protein intake cannot be reached with usual food, the use of high protein nutritional supplements may be considered" (p. 737). Evidence for individual nutrients and for timing should not be overstated (p. 737).

**A. Consider vitamin D on the basis of demonstrated improvement in muscle function in sarcopenia.** Wrong, Vitamin D has not been shown to improve muscle function in sarcopenic patients; a possible benefit in severe deficiency does not establish the claimed general effect (p. 737).
**B. Review food intake and consider high-protein supplements when usual food does not meet requirements.** Correct, This follows the source’s sequence of reviewing food intake and considering supplementation when food does not meet requirements (p. 737).
**C. Consider isolated leucine on the basis of demonstrated effects independent of complete nutritional supplements.** Wrong, Trials generally used complete supplements, so the effect of isolated leucine in older people is described as unknown (p. 737).
**D. Spread additional protein throughout the day in preference to timing a protein boost near exercise.** Wrong, The source favors a timed protein boost and describes avid uptake immediately after exercise, rather than favoring distribution across the day (p. 737).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 737.
label: Source: hazzard marked .pdf · 737

q: An 84-year-old woman with progressive Alzheimer dementia and an MMSE score of 18/30 takes donepezil. Which cardiovascular adverse-effect pattern is identified in Hazzard as potentially serious enough to trigger deprescribing a cholinesterase inhibitor?
o: Hypertension with an increase in heart rate
Bradycardia with an episode of syncope
Tachycardia with accelerated AV conduction
Hypertension with accelerated AV conduction
explanation:
**Bradycardia and syncope** are potentially serious cholinesterase-inhibitor adverse effects. Hazzard also lists AV nodal block and unintentional weight loss as effects that can trigger deprescribing (p. 911). The deciding passage names “Bradycardia, atrioventricular (AV) nodal block, and syncope” (p. 911).

**A. Hypertension with an increase in heart rate.** Wrong, increased heart rate and hypertension do not match the slow-rate and conduction-block pattern described (p. 911).
**B. Bradycardia with an episode of syncope.** Correct, both are explicitly named as potentially serious adverse effects that would trigger deprescribing (p. 911).
**C. Tachycardia with accelerated AV conduction.** Wrong, the described adverse effects include bradycardia and AV nodal block, rather than faster rate and conduction (p. 911).
**D. Hypertension with accelerated AV conduction.** Wrong, accelerated conduction conflicts with the AV nodal block described; hypertension is not the pattern asked for (p. 911).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 911.
label: Source: Hazzard 8e (marked) · p. 911

q: A comprehensive geriatric assessment identifies depression as a contributor to functional decline in a 77-year-old patient. Why is this finding clinically useful?
o: It identifies disability for which management centers on compensatory assistance
It identifies a treatable affective disorder associated with increased disability
It identifies preserved function despite the reported difficulties in daily activities
It identifies dementia as the established explanation for the functional decline
explanation:
**Depression** is a treatable disorder associated with disability and reduced quality of life. Recognizing it identifies a potentially treatable contributor to impairment; the finding does not itself establish dementia or preserved function (p. 123).
"These treatable disorders are associated with increased disability, health care utilization, morbidity, and mortality, and decreased quality of life." (p. 123).

**A. It identifies disability for which management centers on compensatory assistance.** Wrong, The source identifies affective disorders as treatable, so a response centered on compensating for disability misses the treatable disorder identified here (p. 123).
**B. It identifies a treatable affective disorder associated with increased disability.** Correct, This connects the observed functional difficulty with the source-described association between treatable affective disorders and disability (p. 123).
**C. It identifies preserved function despite the reported difficulties in daily activities.** Wrong, The source associates depression with increased disability; its identification does not negate the functional decline in the stem (p. 123).
**D. It identifies dementia as the established explanation for the functional decline.** Wrong, The source discusses depression as an affective disorder that can coexist with cognitive impairment; it does not make depression a diagnosis of dementia (p. 123).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 123.
ref: Hazzard Ch 8 — PRINCIPLES OF GERIATRIC ASSESSMENT

q: According to the 2023 AGS Beers Criteria, which effect supports avoiding concomitant opioid and benzodiazepine use in an older adult?
o: The combination may decrease sedation while depressing respiration
The combination may cause profound sedation and respiratory depression
The combination may cause profound sedation while stimulating respiration
The combination may decrease sedation while stimulating respiration
explanation:
Combining an opioid with a benzodiazepine creates a risk of **profound sedation and respiratory depression**, with potentially fatal outcomes. The Beers Criteria state: "Concomitant use of opioids may result in profound sedation, respiratory depression, coma, and death." (p. 2060).

**A. The combination may decrease sedation while depressing respiration.** Wrong, the source warns of profound sedation, rather than decreased sedation, with concomitant use (p. 2060).
**B. The combination may cause profound sedation and respiratory depression.** Correct, both effects are explicitly listed in the warning about concomitant opioid use (p. 2060).
**C. The combination may cause profound sedation while stimulating respiration.** Wrong, the warning describes respiratory depression, rather than stimulation of respiration (p. 2060).
**D. The combination may decrease sedation while stimulating respiration.** Wrong, both proposed directions conflict with the listed risks of profound sedation and respiratory depression (p. 2060).

Source: AGS Beers 2023, pp. 2060.
ref: Hazzard Ch 22 — MEDICATION PRESCRIBING AND DE-PRESCRIBING

q: A 71-year-old man presents with cognitive decline, visual hallucinations, slow shuffling gait, and frequent falls. He also acts out dreams during REM sleep. Which dementia syndrome is most consistent with this combination?
o: Alzheimer disease with a predominantly episodic-memory syndrome
Nonfluent primary progressive aphasia with an agrammatic syndrome
Dementia with Lewy bodies and associated parkinsonian features
Behavioral-variant frontotemporal dementia with personality change
explanation:
**Dementia with Lewy bodies** combines cognitive decline with characteristic motor, perceptual, and sleep features. Hazzard lists “Fluctuations, visual hallucinations, REM sleep disorder, parkinsonism” as its distinguishing clinical pattern (p. 993). The hallucinations, parkinsonian gait, and dream enactment in the stem align with that pattern.

**A. Alzheimer disease with a predominantly episodic-memory syndrome.** Wrong, episodic-memory decline alone does not account for the distinctive hallucination, REM sleep, and parkinsonian cluster assigned to DLB in the source (p. 993).
**B. Nonfluent primary progressive aphasia with an agrammatic syndrome.** Wrong, nonfluent aphasia is characterized by apraxic speech and agrammatism, which are not the defining symptoms presented here (p. 993).
**C. Dementia with Lewy bodies and associated parkinsonian features.** Correct, this is the syndrome whose source-listed features match the combined cognitive, motor, visual, and sleep presentation (p. 993).
**D. Behavioral-variant frontotemporal dementia with personality change.** Wrong, behavioral-variant FTD is characterized by personality change, loss of empathy, stereotyped behavior, and hyperorality rather than this DLB cluster (p. 993).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 993.
label: Source: Hazzard 8e (marked) · p. 983

q: מה הצפי הדמוגרפי ל-10 שנים קדימה לגבי אנשים בני 65+ בארצות הברית?
o: יישאר על 16% הנוכחיים מהאוכלוסייה
יעלה לכ-20-23% מהאוכלוסייה
יירד עקב ירידה בתוחלת החיים
מבנה הגיל ישקף את הפצ'ות הנוכחית
explanation:
התשובה הנכונה היא B, מכיוון שהתחזיות הדמוגרפיות של ה-U.S. Census Bureau מצביעות באופן עקבי על כך ששיעור המבוגרים בני 65 ומעלה יעלה משמעותית בעשור הקרוב, בעיקר בשל הזדקנות דור ה-Baby Boom (נולדו 1946–1964). כפי שמתואר ב-Hazzard's Principles of Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, ה-"graying of America" משקף את השילוב של תוחלת חיים מוארכת, ירידה בפריון, וגודלו העצום של דור ה-Baby Boom הנכנס לגיל המבוגר. עד אמצע שנות ה-2030, התחזיות מציבות את אוכלוסיית ה-65+ על כ-20–23% מסך אוכלוסיית ארה"ב, לעומת כ-16–17% בשנים האחרונות.

תשובה A שגויה כי שמירה על 16% תדרוש קיפאון דמוגרפי, תוך התעלמות מאפקט הגל המסיבי של ה-Baby Boomers הנכנסים לקטגוריה זו. תשובה C שגויה כי למרות תנודות קלות בתוחלת החיים (למשל בשל COVID-19 ומשבר ה-opioid), המגמות ארוכות הטווח מראות המשך עלייה בתוחלת החיים; אין תחזית אמינה המנבאת ירידה בחלקם של המבוגרים באוכלוסייה. תשובה D שגויה כי מבנה הגיל משתנה באופן פעיל לכיוון אוכלוסייה מבוגרת יותר — ה-dependency ratio עולה, ופירמידת הגיל הופכת מלבנית יותר ואף הפוכה בחלקה העליון.

Clinical Pearl: הבנת מגמות דמוגרפיות חיונית לתכנון כוח אדם רפואי, שכן האוכלוסייה הגדלה של בני 65+ תגדיל באופן דרמטי את הביקוש לרופאים מוכשרים בגריאטריה ולמערכות בריאות age-friendly.

q: A 78-year-old woman reports urine loss when running or coughing and denies sudden urgency or nocturia. Which brief interview instrument was developed to distinguish stress from urge incontinence in women in primary care?
o: Postvoid residual measurement
The 3IQ questionnaire
Multichannel urodynamic testing
Filling cystometrography
explanation:
**The 3IQ questionnaire** distinguishes stress and urge incontinence through a brief interview in primary care. Leakage with physical activity is classified as stress or stress-predominant incontinence; applying that classification to her reported symptoms is an inference (p. 120).
"developed to distinguish between urinary stress and urge incontinence in women in primary care settings" (p. 120).
"instrument with high sensitivity and specificity" (p. 120).

**A. Postvoid residual measurement.** Wrong, this measures retained urine rather than administering the brief interview used for symptom classification (pp. 120, 705).
**B. The 3IQ questionnaire.** Correct, the source identifies this questionnaire as the brief instrument developed for this distinction (p. 120).
**C. Multichannel urodynamic testing.** Wrong, this is a complex urodynamic investigation for selected patients, rather than the brief primary-care interview described (pp. 120, 705).
**D. Filling cystometrography.** Wrong, this measures bladder pressure during filling, rather than eliciting the circumstances of leakage through the specified interview (pp. 120, 562).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 120, 562, 705.

q: A 72-year-old man hospitalized with COPD develops a stage 2 sacral pressure injury on the third hospital day. Which intervention directly addresses continuing pressure exposure and belongs in the treatment plan for an existing pressure injury?
o: Apply topical antibiotic ointment to the sacral wound
Provide pressure relief and repositioning adapted to the patient
Provide supplemental vitamin C to support intake during wound treatment
Apply an enzymatic debridement agent to the sacral wound
explanation:
**Pressure relief and repositioning** remain part of care after a pressure injury has developed. "If pressure is not relieved, the blood vessels collapse and thrombose." (p. 681). Prevention measures also belong in the treatment plan for existing injuries, with repositioning intervals informed by the patient and support surface (p. 683).

**A. Apply topical antibiotic ointment to the sacral wound.** Wrong, an ointment does not implement the pressure-relieving intervention needed to address ongoing mechanical exposure (pp. 681, 683).
**B. Provide pressure relief and repositioning adapted to the patient.** Correct, this addresses the continuing pressure and applies the source’s repositioning and support-surface principles to an existing injury (p. 683).
**C. Provide supplemental vitamin C to support intake during wound treatment.** Wrong, nutritional support is part of care, but a supplement does not substitute for reducing the pressure exposure asked about (pp. 681, 683).
**D. Apply an enzymatic debridement agent to the sacral wound.** Wrong, debridement reduces devitalized or necrotic tissue; it does not substitute for pressure relief and repositioning (pp. 683, 695).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 681, 683, 695.
label: Source: hazzard marked .pdf · 683

q: A 76-year-old woman has a DXA T-score of -2.8 and no previous fragility fracture. Which classification in Hazzard’s WHO criteria table fits these findings?
o: Bone density is classified as normal
Bone density is classified as osteopenia
Bone density is classified as severe osteoporosis
Bone density is classified as osteoporosis
explanation:
**Osteoporosis** in the table is defined by a T-score of -2.5 or lower; severe osteoporosis additionally includes a fragility fracture (p. 760). The table lists "Osteoporosis ≤ −2.5" and "Severe osteoporosis ≤ −2.5 + fragility fracture" (p. 760). Thus, this is a classification question using both bone density and fracture history.

**A. Bone density is classified as normal.** Wrong, the normal category requires a T-score above -1, whereas the stated value is below the osteoporosis threshold (p. 760).
**B. Bone density is classified as osteopenia.** Wrong, the osteopenia row requires a value above -2.5; the stated value falls on the osteoporosis side of that boundary (p. 760).
**C. Bone density is classified as severe osteoporosis.** Wrong, the severe category adds a fragility fracture to the low T-score; that fracture history is absent in the stem (p. 760).
**D. Bone density is classified as osteoporosis.** Correct, the value meets the osteoporosis threshold, and the stem does not supply the additional fragility fracture required for the severe category (p. 760).

Source: Hazzard’s Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th ed., pp. 760.

q: An 82-year-old man with heart failure and reduced ejection fraction is starting spironolactone. Which laboratory measurements require close monitoring during initiation and dose titration?
o: Liver enzyme levels and platelet count
Renal function and serum potassium levels
Vitamin B12 and folate levels
Thyroid hormone and serum ferritin levels
explanation:
**Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists** are potassium-sparing diuretics that interfere with aldosterone. Hazzard identifies significant renal dysfunction and preexisting hyperkalemia as contraindications and emphasizes close monitoring because older patients have increased risk of adverse effects (p. 1181). "renal function and serum potassium levels should be monitored closely during initiation and titration of therapy" (p. 1181).

**A. Liver enzyme levels and platelet count.** Wrong, These measurements do not provide the renal function and potassium monitoring specified for this potassium-sparing treatment (p. 1181).
**B. Renal function and serum potassium levels.** Correct, Both measurements are explicitly required during initiation and titration of this therapy (p. 1181).
**C. Vitamin B12 and folate levels.** Wrong, These measurements leave the renal dysfunction and potassium risks highlighted in the source unmonitored (p. 1181).
**D. Thyroid hormone and serum ferritin levels.** Wrong, These measurements do not assess the renal function or potassium changes that the source directs clinicians to monitor (p. 1181).

Source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th ed., pp. 1181.
ref: Hazzard Ch 76 — HEART FAILURE · Harrison Ch 316 — Cardiogenic Shock and Pulmonary Edema

q: An overweight woman with knee osteoarthritis asks for a treatment plan that includes weight loss. Which approach matches the chapter recommendations?
o: Rapid weight loss through a crash diet with reduced physical activity
Gradual weight loss combined with aerobic and strengthening exercise
Maintenance of current weight combined with aerobic and strengthening exercise
Gradual weight loss combined with avoidance of strengthening exercise
explanation:
**Weight reduction and exercise** are recommended for overweight patients with knee osteoarthritis. A program should support gradual, sustained weight loss, while aerobic activity and muscle strengthening can improve symptoms and physical health (pp. 784, 786).
"Aerobic exercise and muscle strengthening can significantly improve the physical health and symptoms of patients with OA." (p. 784).
"All existing guidelines highly recommend weight loss in overweight and obese individuals with OA of the hip or knee for OA management." (p. 786).

**A. Rapid weight loss through a crash diet with reduced physical activity.** Wrong, the source advises avoiding fad diets and building healthy physical activity habits rather than combining rapid loss with less activity (p. 786).
**B. Gradual weight loss combined with aerobic and strengthening exercise.** Correct, this combines the recommended gradual weight loss with the two exercise components described (pp. 784, 786).
**C. Maintenance of current weight combined with aerobic and strengthening exercise.** Wrong, exercise is appropriate, but retaining excess weight omits the recommended weight-loss component (p. 786).
**D. Gradual weight loss combined with avoidance of strengthening exercise.** Wrong, avoiding strengthening omits a treatment that can improve physical health and symptoms (p. 784).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 784, 786.
ref: Hazzard Ch 52 — OSTEOARTHRITIS · Harrison Ch 382 — Approach to Articular and Musculoskeletal Disease

q: An 80-year-old patient taking chronic morphine for cancer pain develops fecal impaction. Which effect of enteric mu-opioid receptor activation explains the constipation?
o: Increased bowel contractility with increased colonic fluid absorption
Decreased bowel contractility with increased colonic fluid absorption
Decreased bowel contractility with decreased colonic fluid absorption
Increased bowel contractility with decreased colonic fluid absorption
explanation:
**Enteric mu-opioid receptor activation** impairs stool passage through effects on bowel movement, fluid absorption, and sphincter tone. The source describes "a decrease in" bowel tone and contractility, followed by "an increase in colonic fluid absorption and anal sphincter tone" (pp. 1377–1378). These effects make stool more difficult to pass (p. 1378).

**A. Increased bowel contractility with increased colonic fluid absorption.** Wrong, The source describes decreased bowel contractility, so increased contractility does not match the opioid effect (pp. 1377–1378).
**B. Decreased bowel contractility with increased colonic fluid absorption.** Correct, Decreased contractility and increased colonic fluid absorption are both part of the described mechanism of difficult stool passage (pp. 1377–1378).
**C. Decreased bowel contractility with decreased colonic fluid absorption.** Wrong, The source describes increased fluid absorption; decreased absorption is not the opioid effect described here (p. 1378).
**D. Increased bowel contractility with decreased colonic fluid absorption.** Wrong, The source describes decreased contractility together with increased fluid absorption, rather than the two proposed directions (pp. 1377–1378).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 1377, 1378.
label: Source: Hazzard 8e (marked) · pp. 1377–1378

q: A 74-year-old man requests treatment for insomnia and asks about lorazepam. Which statement explains the Beers 2023 warning about benzodiazepines in older adults?
o: Choosing a short-acting agent reduces the risk of subsequent falls
Older adults have increased sensitivity and an increased risk of falls
Continued benzodiazepine use reduces the risk of physical dependence
Combining a benzodiazepine with an opioid reduces the risk of sedation
explanation:
**Benzodiazepine sensitivity** is increased in older adults, and this drug class increases the risk of falls and cognitive adverse effects. Short duration of action does not make a benzodiazepine safer for falls; continued use also carries a risk of physical dependence (pp. 2060, 2066).
"Older adults have increased sensitivity to benzodiazepines and decreased metabolism of long-acting agents;" (p. 2060).
"In general, all benzodiazepines increase the risk of cognitive impairment, delirium, falls, fractures, and motor vehicle crashes in older adults." (p. 2060).

**A. Choosing a short-acting agent reduces the risk of subsequent falls.** Wrong, Beers specifically states that shorter-acting benzodiazepines are not safer than long-acting ones in people with a history of falls or fractures (p. 2066).
**B. Older adults have increased sensitivity and an increased risk of falls.** Correct, Beers identifies increased sensitivity in older adults and includes falls among the risks of this drug class (p. 2060).
**C. Continued benzodiazepine use reduces the risk of physical dependence.** Wrong, continued use may lead to clinically significant physical dependence rather than protecting against it (p. 2060).
**D. Combining a benzodiazepine with an opioid reduces the risk of sedation.** Wrong, concomitant opioid use can cause profound sedation and respiratory depression, rather than reducing sedation (p. 2060).

Source: 2023 AGS Beers Criteria, pp. 2060, 2066.
ref: Hazzard Ch 22 — MEDICATION PRESCRIBING AND DE-PRESCRIBING

q: An older woman with long-standing hypertension develops dizziness when her blood pressure falls abruptly after a treatment change. Why can cerebral ischemic symptoms occur even within a blood pressure range considered normal?
o: The cerebral autoregulatory threshold shifts toward lower pressures
The cerebral autoregulatory threshold shifts toward higher pressures
The abrupt pressure fall increases cerebral blood flow
Acute antihypertensive administration protects against postural hypotension
explanation:
In older adults with hypertension, **cerebral autoregulation** is shifted toward higher blood pressures. Cerebral blood flow can consequently fall during a sudden pressure decline even within the normal range; acute antihypertensive administration in impaired regulation can further increase orthostatic hypotension and syncope risk (p. 668).
"the threshold for cerebral autoregulation is shifted to higher blood pressures." (p. 668).
"This may result in decreased cerebral blood flow at higher blood pressure values," (p. 668).

**A. The cerebral autoregulatory threshold shifts toward lower pressures.** Wrong, A lower threshold does not explain the vulnerability described: the source places the threshold at higher pressures (p. 668).
**B. The cerebral autoregulatory threshold shifts toward higher pressures.** Correct, The higher threshold makes a sudden pressure fall capable of reducing cerebral blood flow even at otherwise normal pressures (p. 668).
**C. The abrupt pressure fall increases cerebral blood flow.** Wrong, The source describes decreased cerebral blood flow during this pressure decline, accounting for ischemic symptoms (p. 668).
**D. Acute antihypertensive administration protects against postural hypotension.** Wrong, In impaired regulation, acute administration can increase orthostatic hypotension and syncope risk rather than protect against them (p. 668).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 668.
ref: Hazzard Ch 79 — HYPERTENSION · Harrison Ch 243 — Approach to the Patient with Possible Cardiovascular Disease

q: An 84-year-old patient has exertional dyspnea, orthopnea, preserved ejection fraction, and echocardiographic evidence of elevated filling pressures. Which treatment principle agrees with the discussion of heart failure with preserved ejection fraction in Hazzard?
o: Prioritize beta-blockade to improve the ability to increase heart rate during exercise
Prioritize symptom relief and blood-pressure control with diuretics titrated to congestion
Prioritize rapid diuresis to reduce filling volume despite emerging relative hypotension
Prioritize avoiding diuretics because preserved ejection fraction makes congestion unresponsive
explanation:
**Congestion and blood pressure** are central treatment targets in the cited discussion. Hazzard calls diuretics "an essential component of therapy for the relief of pulmonary and systemic venous congestion" (p. 1186). Patients may be volume sensitive, so symptom relief requires judicious titration rather than excessive volume depletion (p. 1186).

**A. Prioritize beta-blockade to improve the ability to increase heart rate during exercise.** Wrong, Chronotropic incompetence is common in this condition and may be exacerbated by beta-blockers; the source does not support choosing them to improve the exercise heart-rate response (p. 1186).
**B. Prioritize symptom relief and blood-pressure control with diuretics titrated to congestion.** Correct, This combines management of hypertension with relief of congestion, while respecting the source warning to avoid overdiuresis (p. 1186).
**C. Prioritize rapid diuresis to reduce filling volume despite emerging relative hypotension.** Wrong, Excessive diuresis can reduce ventricular filling volume, stroke volume, and cardiac output, producing hypotension and prerenal azotemia (p. 1186).
**D. Prioritize avoiding diuretics because preserved ejection fraction makes congestion unresponsive.** Wrong, The source specifically identifies diuretics as essential for congestion in most patients with preserved ejection fraction; preserved systolic function does not justify withholding them for that reason (p. 1186).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 1186.
ref: Hazzard Ch 77 — CARDIAC ARRHYTHMIAS · Harrison Ch 316 — Cardiogenic Shock and Pulmonary Edema

q: A 75-year-old man has diabetic neuropathic pain, normal renal function, and no concurrent opioid treatment. Gabapentin is started at 100 mg at bedtime as listed in Table 68-8. Which titration approach follows that table?
o: Advance to the maintenance dose immediately after the first bedtime dose
Increase the dose gradually, guided by response and tolerability
Introduce concurrent oxycodone as the gabapentin dose is increased
Replace low-dose initiation with immediate maintenance-dose treatment
explanation:
**Low-dose initiation and gradual titration** are the table’s principles for gabapentinoids (p. 1063). It states "Initiate at lowest dose and gradually titrate" and cautions against concurrent opioid use; central nervous system adverse effects also require attention (pp. 1063–1064).

**A. Advance to the maintenance dose immediately after the first bedtime dose.** Wrong, an immediate increase to maintenance dosing conflicts with the table’s gradual titration instruction (p. 1063).
**B. Increase the dose gradually, guided by response and tolerability.** Correct, gradual adjustment follows the stated approach, with response and adverse effects informing the clinical application (pp. 1063–1064).
**C. Introduce concurrent oxycodone as the gabapentin dose is increased.** Wrong, the table advises avoiding gabapentinoids in patients with concurrent opioid use, so introducing oxycodone conflicts with that instruction (p. 1063).
**D. Replace low-dose initiation with immediate maintenance-dose treatment.** Wrong, immediate maintenance-dose treatment abandons both low-dose initiation and gradual titration (p. 1063).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 1063, 1064.
ref: Hazzard Ch 68 — PAIN MANAGEMENT · Harrison Ch 14 — Pain: Pathophysiology and Management

q: A 79-year-old woman with coronary artery disease and a previous myocardial infarction takes a high-intensity statin. She tolerates it well and has good functional status. Which approach is appropriate according to Hazzard?
o: Consider stopping the statin because secondary prevention lacks benefit at her age
Consider continuing the tolerated statin for secondary prevention of recurrent cardiovascular events
Consider stopping the statin because primary prevention has uncertain benefit at her age
Consider replacing the statin with fish oil as proven therapy for secondary prevention
explanation:
**Secondary prevention** with statins reduces major vascular events in older adults, including those aged 75 or older. Hazzard considers continuation of a **high-intensity statin** reasonable in this age group when it is tolerated (p. 1141). Her previous myocardial infarction places this scenario in secondary prevention; uncertainty about primary prevention does not describe this clinical setting (application of p. 1141).
"it is reasonable to continue high-intensity statin in patients aged 75 or older if tolerated." (p. 1141).
"for secondary prevention of ASCVD, moderate-intensity statin use reduces major vascular events including in those aged 75 or older." (p. 1141).

**A. Consider stopping the statin because secondary prevention lacks benefit at her age.** Wrong, The source reports secondary-prevention benefit in people aged 75 or older, so the proposed absence of benefit conflicts with the evidence it describes (p. 1141).
**B. Consider continuing the tolerated statin for secondary prevention of recurrent cardiovascular events.** Correct, She has established coronary disease and tolerates treatment; continuing high-intensity therapy fits the recommendation for tolerated treatment after age 75 (p. 1141).
**C. Consider stopping the statin because primary prevention has uncertain benefit at her age.** Wrong, The uncertainty discussed concerns primary prevention. Applying it to a patient with a previous myocardial infarction confuses that setting with the supported secondary-prevention indication (p. 1141).
**D. Consider replacing the statin with fish oil as proven therapy for secondary prevention.** Wrong, Among the lipid-lowering therapies discussed, the source identifies statins, alone or with ezetimibe or PCSK9 inhibitors, as having proven secondary-prevention efficacy; it does not establish fish oil as their replacement (p. 1141).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 1141.
ref: Hazzard Ch 74 — CORONARY HEART DISEASE AND DYSLIPIDEMIA · Harrison Ch 286 — ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction

q: A 73-year-old woman who has taken alendronate for several years reports new atraumatic thigh and groin pain. Which investigation is directed at a suspected atypical femoral fracture associated with prolonged treatment?
o: Bone-density measurement to assess bone mass
Plain radiography of the painful femoral region
Serum calcium measurement to assess mineral balance
Bone-turnover markers to assess skeletal response
explanation:
**Atypical femoral fracture** is associated with prolonged bisphosphonate treatment (p. 776). The source says it "should be investigated with x-ray in patients complaining of groin or thigh pain"; this targets the suspected fracture rather than general bone status (p. 776).

**A. Bone-density measurement to assess bone mass.** Wrong, bone-density assessment does not perform the fracture-directed radiographic investigation specified for this presentation (p. 776).
**B. Plain radiography of the painful femoral region.** Correct, radiography is the investigation explicitly recommended for groin or thigh pain during prolonged bisphosphonate use (p. 776).
