q: גבר בן 78 עם דמנציה וסקולרית, CKD stage 3b (eGFR 35), ושבר ירך לאחרונה, משוחרר מאשפוז שיקומי. ה-MoCA שלו הוא 16/30. בתו רוצה שישוב הביתה אליה; בנו מתעקש על מעבר לבית אבות. המטופל אומר 'אני רוצה ללכת הביתה עם מרי [הבת]' אך אינו מסוגל להסביר כיצד תעזור לו או מה בדיוק הוא צריך. הפיזיותרפיסט מציין שהוא זקוק להשגחה בכל העברות ונפל פעמיים במהלך הטיפול. הוא נוטל warfarin בגלל AFib והחסיר מספר מנות במהלך האשפוז. איזה גורם תומך בצורה החזקה ביותר בצורך באפוטרופסות?
o: ציון MoCA המצביע על דמנציה בינונית
חוסר יכולת לנהל anticoagulation בבטחה
חוסר הסכמה משפחתית לגבי המיקום
חוסר יכולת להסביר את צרכי הטיפול למרות הבעת העדפה
explanation:
הערכת צורך באפוטרופסות צריכה להבחין בין **קושי לבצע מטלות** לבין **קושי לקבל החלטות עליהן**. החוק נותן משקל ליכולת לקבל החלטות ולסיוע הזמין, ומחייב לבחון חלופות המגבילות פחות את הזכויות לפני מינוי (עמ׳ 44–45, סעיף 33א). כהסקה מן ההבחנה הזאת, חוסר היכולת להסביר את צרכי הטיפול למרות הבעת העדפה הוא הרמז הממוקד ביותר לצורך בבירור; הוא אינו מספיק לבדו להחלטה על מינוי.
"לא ימנה בית המשפט אפוטרופוס לאדם שאינו מסוגל לדאוג לענייניו אך מסוגל לקבל החלטות בקשר אליהם, אלא בנסיבות מיוחדות" (עמ׳ 45, סעיף 33א(ב)).

**א. ציון MoCA המצביע על דמנציה בינונית.** שגויה, ציון במבחן אינו מתאר אם האדם יכול לקבל את החלטת המגורים בעזרת תמיכה. כהסקה מדרישת החוק לבחון יכולת וסיוע בפועל, הציון לבדו אינו מבסס צורך במינוי (עמ׳ 44–45, סעיף 33א).
**ב. חוסר יכולת לנהל anticoagulation בבטחה.** שגויה, קושי בביצוע טיפול תרופתי מדגים צורך בעזרה, אך אינו מוכיח שאין דרך לספק את העזרה בלי אפוטרופוס. החוק מחייב לבחון חלופות וסיוע לאדם שיכול לקבל החלטות (עמ׳ 44–45, סעיף 33א).
**ג. חוסר הסכמה משפחתית לגבי המיקום.** שגויה, מחלוקת בין בני משפחה אינה אחד התנאים המספיקים למינוי. יש לברר את יכולת האדם ואת האפשרות לשמור על ענייניו בדרך פחות מגבילה (עמ׳ 44–45, סעיף 33א).
**ד. חוסר יכולת להסביר את צרכי הטיפול למרות הבעת העדפה.** נכונה, כהסקה מן התיאור, הפער בין בחירה לבין הבנת צורכי הטיפול מעורר את השאלה אם הוא מסוגל להחליט בענייניו. זה רלוונטי יותר מהציון או המחלוקת כשלעצמם, אך עדיין מחייב הערכה ובחינת חלופות (עמ׳ 44–45, סעיף 33א).

מקור: חוק הכשרות המשפטית והאפוטרופסות, סעיפים 33 ו־33א, עמ׳ 44–45 בעותק המקור.

q: מטופלת מאושפזת בישראל מוגדרת חסרת ישע. בבירור עולה חשד שהאדם האחראי עליה פוגע בה. איזה צעד מתחייב לפי נוהל משרד הבריאות?
o: מסירת הודעה מיידית לפקיד סעד או למשטרה על החשד
דחיית ההודעה עד לפגישה משותפת עם המטפל ועם המשפחה
המתנה לאימות סופי של האירוע לפני העברת הודעה לגורם חיצוני
הסתפקות במעקב מחלקתי ובתיעוד במקום מסירת הודעה חיצונית
explanation:
**הודעה על חשד לפגיעה** בחסר ישע בידי האחראי עליו נמסרת מיידית לפקיד סעד או למשטרה. הנוהל מציב פעולה זו במסגרת בירור החשד והגנה על הנפגע; אין להחליף את מסלול ההודעה בדיון משפחתי או במעקב בלבד (עמ׳ 6).
"כאשר הפגיעה בחסר ישע היא על ידי המטפל העיקרי או אדם אחר האחראי עליו לפי ההגדרה שלעיל, תימסר מיידית הודעה לפקיד סעד ו/או למשטרה." (עמ׳ 6).

**א. מסירת הודעה מיידית לפקיד סעד או למשטרה על החשד.** נכונה, זהו מסלול ההודעה המיידית שהנוהל קובע בחשד לפגיעה בחסר ישע בידי האחראי עליו (עמ׳ 6).
**ב. דחיית ההודעה עד לפגישה משותפת עם המטפל ועם המשפחה.** שגויה, פגישה עשויה להיות חלק מהטיפול, אך אינה מחליפה או דוחה את ההודעה המיידית בנסיבות המתוארות (עמ׳ 6).
**ג. המתנה לאימות סופי של האירוע לפני העברת הודעה לגורם חיצוני.** שגויה, הנוהל פועל במסגרת בירור חשד להתעמרות ומורה על הודעה מיידית; אין להמיר זאת בהמתנה לאימות סופי (עמ׳ 6).
**ד. הסתפקות במעקב מחלקתי ובתיעוד במקום מסירת הודעה חיצונית.** שגויה, תיעוד ומעקב אינם ממלאים את חובת מסירת ההודעה לגורמים שצוינו בנוהל (עמ׳ 6).

מקור: משרד הבריאות, נוהל טיפול בזקנים נפגעי התעמרות, סעיף 8.5, עמ׳ 6.

q: מטופל באשפוז ממושך מופנה להערכת צורך באפוטרופוס. הצוות מכין את התעודה הרפואית הנדרשת בהליך המתואר בחוזר משרד הבריאות. מי צריך לערוך את התעודה?
o: רופא כללי המכיר את המשפחה ללא מומחיות
עובד סוציאלי המכיר את המשפחה ואת מצבה
רופא מומחה מאחד התחומים המנויים בחוזר
בן משפחה המכיר את המטופל ומלווה אותו
explanation:
**בקשה למינוי אפוטרופוס** נשענת על תיעוד רפואי מתאים, ולא על עצם קיומן של נפילות או אבחנת דמנציה. החוזר דורש תעודה של רופא מומחה מאחד התחומים המנויים בו וממליץ על מומחיות הרלוונטית למחלות המחייבות את הבירור (סעיף 9.3.1, עמ׳ 4).
"תעודת רופא מומחה תיערך ע"י רופא, שהוא מומחה באחד התחומים הבאים:" (עמ׳ 4).

**א. רופא כללי המכיר את המשפחה ללא מומחיות.** שגויה, החוזר דורש רופא מומחה; היכרות ללא מומחיות אינה ממלאת את הדרישה לתעודה (עמ׳ 4).
**ב. עובד סוציאלי המכיר את המשפחה ואת מצבה.** שגויה, לעובד הסוציאלי יש תפקיד בדוח הסוציאלי, אך הוא אינו מחליף את תעודת הרופא המומחה (עמ׳ 4).
**ג. רופא מומחה מאחד התחומים המנויים בחוזר.** נכונה, זו הדרישה המפורשת לתעודה הרפואית, כחלק ממסמכי הבקשה (עמ׳ 4).
**ד. בן משפחה המכיר את המטופל ומלווה אותו.** שגויה, היכרות משפחתית אינה מחליפה את הבדיקה והתעודה של רופא מומחה הנדרשות בהליך (עמ׳ 4).

מקור: חוזר מינוי אפוטרופוס באשפוז ממושך, סעיף 9.3.1, עמ׳ 4.
ref: Hazzard Ch 26 — LEGAL ISSUES· Harrison Ch 433 — Approach to the Patient with Neurologic Disease

q: לפי סעיף 2 לחוק הכשרות המשפטית והאפוטרופסות, איזה מצב מהווה חריג לברירת המחדל של כשרות אדם לפעולות משפטיות?
o: כאשר נרשמה אבחנה קוגניטיבית בתיק הרפואי
כאשר הכשרות נשללה בחוק או בפסק דין
כאשר בני המשפחה חולקים על ההחלטה שקיבל
כאשר הפעולה חורגת מהעדפותיו הקודמות
explanation:
**כשרות לפעולות משפטיות** היא ברירת המחדל שקובע החוק. שלילה או הגבלה נעשות בחוק או בפסק דין; מכאן שאין להסיק שלילת כשרות מהאבחנה או ממחלוקת משפחתית כשלעצמן, והסקה זו אינה תחליף לבדיקת הפעולה המסוימת (סעיף 2, עמ׳ 1).
"כל אדם כשר לפעולות משפטיות, זולת אם נשללה או הוגבלה כשרות זו בחוק או בפסק דין של בית משפט." (עמ׳ 1).

**א. כאשר נרשמה אבחנה קוגניטיבית בתיק הרפואי.** שגויה, אבחנה בתיק אינה אחת מדרכי שלילת הכשרות המנויות בסעיף; אין להסיק ממנה לבדה שהכשרות נשללה (עמ׳ 1).
**ב. כאשר הכשרות נשללה בחוק או בפסק דין.** נכונה, זהו הכלל המפורש בסעיף 2, והוא מבחין בין ברירת המחדל לבין שלילה או הגבלה משפטית (עמ׳ 1).
**ג. כאשר בני המשפחה חולקים על ההחלטה שקיבל.** שגויה, מחלוקת משפחתית אינה שלילה בחוק או בפסק דין, ולכן אינה מבטלת את ברירת המחדל (עמ׳ 1).
**ד. כאשר הפעולה חורגת מהעדפותיו הקודמות.** שגויה, שינוי העדפה אינו כשלעצמו שלילה בחוק או בפסק דין; אין בו בסיס אוטומטי לשלול כשרות לפי סעיף זה (עמ׳ 1).

מקור: חוק הכשרות המשפטית והאפוטרופסות, תשכ_ב-1962.pdf, עמ׳ 1.

q: מטופל מבוגר שוקל טיפול רפואי בעל אופי חדשני במסגרת מחקר. בשיחה על הסכמה מדעת, איזה פרט מחייב סעיף 13 לציין, נוסף לתועלת, לסיכונים ולחלופות?
o: את צורכי השלמת הנתונים כתחליף לתיאור החדשנות
את עובדת היות הטיפול המוצע בעל אופי חדשני
את תמיכת המשפחה כתחליף לתיאור החדשנות
את העדפת החוקר כתחליף לתיאור החדשנות
explanation:
**אופיו החדשני של הטיפול** הוא חלק מהמידע שהחוק מונה לצורך הסכמה מדעת. מסירת המידע צריכה לאפשר הבנה ובחירה חופשית; תמיכת קרובים או צורכי המחקר אינם מחליפים מידע זה למטופל (עמ׳ 8, סעיף 13).
"עובדת היות הטיפול בעל אופי חדשני." (עמ׳ 8).
"באופן שיאפשר למטופל מידה מרבית של הבנת המידע לשם קבלת החלטה בדרך של בחירה מרצון ואי תלות." (עמ׳ 8).

**א. את צורכי השלמת הנתונים כתחליף לתיאור החדשנות.** שגויה, שלמות נתונים אינה הפרט שהחוק דורש ואינה תחליף להסבר על חדשנות הטיפול (עמ׳ 8).
**ב. את עובדת היות הטיפול המוצע בעל אופי חדשני.** נכונה, זהו פרט המידע הנוסף המנוי במפורש בחוק (עמ׳ 8).
**ג. את תמיכת המשפחה כתחליף לתיאור החדשנות.** שגויה, תמיכת המשפחה אינה מתארת את אופי הטיפול ואינה ממלאת את חובת הגילוי (עמ׳ 8).
**ד. את העדפת החוקר כתחליף לתיאור החדשנות.** שגויה, העדפת החוקר אינה גילוי של עובדת החדשנות הנדרשת למטופל (עמ׳ 8).

מקור: חוק זכויות החולה, תשנ_ו-1996.pdf, עמ׳ 8.

q: בת 86 בישראל נוהגת למרות ליקוי ראייה קבוע והפרעה קוגניטיבית. הרופא מעריך שמצבה עלול לסכן אותה או אחרים בנהיגה. מה הפעולה המתאימה לפי חוזר מנכ״ל 6/2023?
o: לדווח למרב״ד ולהמליץ להפסיק נהיגה עד הבדיקה
להמתין להסכמת בני המשפחה לפני מסירת הדיווח למרב״ד
למסור תיעוד למשפחה ולהעביר אליה את ההחלטה על דיווח
להימנע מדיווח למרב״ד בשל חובת שמירת הסודיות הרפואית
explanation:
**חובת הדיווח למרב״ד** חלה כאשר הרופא סבור שהמצב הרפואי עלול לסכן בנהיגה, והיא גוברת על הסודיות בנסיבות המתוארות. במקביל יש להזהיר מפני הנהיגה ולהמליץ להפסיקה עד הבדיקה; הדיווח כשלעצמו אינו פסילת רישיון מיידית (עמ׳ 2–3).
"החובה החוקית המפורשת למסירת הודעה למרב"ד, במקרה שהרופא סבור שהאדם עלול לסכן את עצמו או זולתו, גוברת על חובת שמירת הסודיות הרפואית" (עמ׳ 2).

**א. לדווח למרב״ד ולהמליץ להפסיק נהיגה עד הבדיקה.** נכונה, כך משולבים הדיווח הנדרש וההמלצה להימנע מנהיגה עד לבירור במרב״ד (עמ׳ 2–3).
**ב. להמתין להסכמת בני המשפחה לפני מסירת הדיווח למרב״ד.** שגויה, החובה המתוארת היא של הרופא ולא מותנית בהסכמת המשפחה (עמ׳ 2).
**ג. למסור תיעוד למשפחה ולהעביר אליה את ההחלטה על דיווח.** שגויה, העברת התיעוד למשפחה אינה ממלאת את חובת מסירת ההודעה למרב״ד (עמ׳ 2).
**ד. להימנע מדיווח למרב״ד בשל חובת שמירת הסודיות הרפואית.** שגויה, החוזר קובע במפורש שבנסיבות אלה חובת הדיווח גוברת על חובת הסודיות (עמ׳ 2).

מקור: 10Redefiningtheobligation.pdf עמ׳ 2; 10Redefiningtheobligation.pdf עמ׳ 3.

q: גבר בן 77 מתקשה להבין עסקה כספית מסוכנת אך ממשיך לקבל החלטות רפואיות. לאחר בחינת חלופות נקבע שיש צורך באפוטרופוס לעניין הכספי. איזה עיקרון ינחה את היקף המינוי לפי חוק הכשרות המשפטית והאפוטרופסות?
o: התאמת היקף המינוי לכלל האבחנות הרפואיות של האדם
התאמת היקף המינוי לצורך בניהול מרוכז של ענייני האדם
התאמת העניינים והתקופה לצורך שנקבע ולמטרת המינוי
התאמת היקף המינוי להעדפת המשפחה לקבל סמכות רחבה
explanation:
**מינוי אפוטרופוס** אינו מחייב מסירת כל תחומי החיים לניהול אחר. החוק דורש לצמצם ככל האפשר את העניינים ואת התקופה, כאשר אפשר להשיג כך את מטרת המינוי ולשמור על טובת האדם; במקרה זה הצורך שנקבע הוא בתחום הכספי (סעיף 33א, עמ׳ 46).
"יצמצם בית המשפט ככל האפשר את העניינים שיימסרו לאפוטרופוס אם ניתן להשיג את המטרה שלשמה מונה האפוטרופוס ולשמור על טובתו של האדם בלי לקבוע עניינים נוספים." (עמ׳ 46).

**א. התאמת היקף המינוי לכלל האבחנות הרפואיות של האדם.** שגויה, החוק מחייב להתאים את העניינים למטרת המינוי, ולא להרחיב אותם על פי רשימת האבחנות; זהו היסק מעקרון הצמצום (עמ׳ 46).
**ב. התאמת היקף המינוי לצורך בניהול מרוכז של ענייני האדם.** שגויה, נוחות של ניהול מרוכז אינה מחליפה את החובה לצמצם את העניינים כדי להשיג את מטרת המינוי (עמ׳ 46).
**ג. התאמת העניינים והתקופה לצורך שנקבע ולמטרת המינוי.** נכונה, זהו עיקרון הצמצום של החוק: להתאים את העניינים ואת משך המינוי למטרתו (עמ׳ 46).
**ד. התאמת היקף המינוי להעדפת המשפחה לקבל סמכות רחבה.** שגויה, העדפת המשפחה לסמכות רחבה אינה מחליפה את החובה לצמצם לפי מטרת המינוי וטובת האדם (עמ׳ 46).

מקור: חוק הכשרות המשפטית והאפוטרופסות, סעיף 33א, עמ׳ 46.

q: A 78-year-old man with diabetes and mild cognitive impairment has lost weight because of missed meals and low intake. Nutritional assessment finds that dietary restrictions are making intake difficult; he has no swallowing problem. Which plan is appropriate?
o: Increase dietary restrictions and concentrate food into one large meal
Reduce dietary restrictions and provide assistance with small meals
Increase dietary restrictions and reduce the number of daily meals
Reduce food variety and avoid snacks between regular meals
explanation:
**Improving oral intake** includes addressing food preferences, offering frequent small meals and snacks, providing mealtime assistance, and minimizing dietary restrictions. These measures address the intake barriers described in the stem (p. 427).
"providing frequent small meals and snacks" (p. 427).

**A. Increase dietary restrictions and concentrate food into one large meal.** Wrong, this increases restrictions and removes the frequent small meals recommended for poor intake (p. 427).
**B. Reduce dietary restrictions and provide assistance with small meals.** Correct, this combines two source-supported approaches to the stated intake barriers (p. 427).
**C. Increase dietary restrictions and reduce the number of daily meals.** Wrong, fewer meals and additional restrictions conflict with the recommended frequent meals and minimized restrictions (p. 427).
**D. Reduce food variety and avoid snacks between regular meals.** Wrong, the source supports food preferences and snacks rather than restricting variety and snacks (p. 427).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 427.
ref: Hazzard Ch 30 — NUTRITION DISORDERS, OBESITY , AND ENTERAL/PARENTERAL ALIMENTATION · Harrison Ch 50 — Unintentional Weight Loss
chapterTitle: NUTRITION DISORDERS, OBESITY , AND ENTERAL/PARENTERAL ALIMENTATION

q: An older woman with falls takes antihypertensive medication and zolpidem for sleep. Which principle applies to zolpidem in her falls assessment?
o: Increase its dosage to prevent falls attributed to fragmented sleep
Review its ongoing need during the falls risk assessment
Exclude it from review because the fall occurred after sleep
Prioritize it as treatment for falls before nonpharmacologic sleep care
explanation:
**Centrally acting medications** warrant attention in falls assessment. Hazzard states, "Centrally acting medications have consistently been shown to increase fall risk." (p. 639). It advises avoiding Z-drug prescriptions for insomnia in older people, with exceptions for addiction or inability to complete withdrawal, and considering nonpharmacologic management (p. 639).

**A. Increase its dosage to prevent falls attributed to fragmented sleep.** Wrong, increasing a fall-risk-associated sleep medication is not the management principle described for this problem (p. 639).
**B. Review its ongoing need during the falls risk assessment.** Correct, this evaluates an exposure included in the source’s concern about centrally acting medication and Z-drugs, without asserting that it caused every fall (p. 639).
**C. Exclude it from review because the fall occurred after sleep.** Wrong, the timing after sleep does not remove the medication from the source’s fall-risk concern; that exclusion is unsupported (p. 639).
**D. Prioritize it as treatment for falls before nonpharmacologic sleep care.** Wrong, the source advises consideration of nonpharmacologic insomnia management rather than using the Z-drug as a falls treatment (p. 639).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 639.
ref: Hazzard Ch 43 — FALLS · Harrison Ch 26 — Neurologic Causes of Weakness and Paralysis

q: A 79-year-old man with heart failure and cognitive impairment struggles with a complex medication regimen after discharge. Review identifies nonessential drugs and administration times that can be combined. Which structural change follows Hazzard's prescribing principles?
o: Add separate administration times to create more reminders
Retain nonessential medications to preserve familiar habits
Remove nonessential medications and combine administration times
Separate administration times to practice independent management
explanation:
**Regimen complexity** is associated with poorer adherence and more adverse medication effects. Hazzard recommends the simplest effective regimen and discontinuation of unnecessary drugs; the stem specifies that the identified administration times can be combined (pp. 313–314). "The goal should thus be to implement the simplest regimen that controls the patient’s symptoms and illnesses, and optimizes disease prevention." (p. 313).

**A. Add separate administration times to create more reminders.** Wrong, adding administration times increases complexity rather than implementing the simplest effective regimen (p. 313).
**B. Retain nonessential medications to preserve familiar habits.** Wrong, preserving nonessential drugs conflicts with the instruction to consider discontinuing unnecessary drugs (p. 314).
**C. Remove nonessential medications and combine administration times.** Correct, this removes unnecessary treatment and reduces complexity where the review has established that consolidation is feasible (pp. 313–314).
**D. Separate administration times to practice independent management.** Wrong, splitting feasible shared times increases complexity, which the source links to poorer adherence and more adverse effects (p. 313).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 313, 314.
ref: Hazzard Ch 76 — HEART FAILURE · Harrison Ch 316 — Cardiogenic Shock and Pulmonary Edema

q: An 81-year-old woman has lost about 8 lb and feels fatigued over recent months. She lives with her daughter, who works full time, and spends most days alone watching television and eating microwave meals. BMI is 19.5 and albumin 3.1 g/dL; PHQ-2 is negative, and the Berkman-Syme social network index indicates marked isolation. Which plan directly addresses mealtime isolation as part of nutritional care?
o: Provide oral nutritional supplements to consume alone at home.
Arrange delivered meals to consume alone at home.
Provide an appetite stimulant while maintaining solitary meals.
Arrange shared lunches through a senior-center meal program.
explanation:
**Mealtime companionship** is relevant to nutritional care: the source associates eating alone with lower energy intake and social company with greater nutrient intake. Applying that principle, shared meals address the isolation described without claiming they are proven to be the most effective intervention for this patient (p. 410). "Eating alone may be associated with a lower energy intake, and the presence of family and close friends leads to greater nutrient intake." (p. 410).

**A. Provide oral nutritional supplements to consume alone at home.** Wrong, supplementation may address intake, but consuming it alone leaves the identified mealtime isolation unchanged (p. 410; inference).
**B. Arrange delivered meals to consume alone at home.** Wrong, delivery may provide food, but the stated solitary setting does not address mealtime companionship (p. 410; inference).
**C. Provide an appetite stimulant while maintaining solitary meals.** Wrong, maintaining solitary meals leaves the social issue unchanged; Hazzard also notes that appetite stimulants such as cyproheptadine have not shown effectiveness in older adults (pp. 410, 428).
**D. Arrange shared lunches through a senior-center meal program.** Correct, shared lunches provide company at meals, directly applying the source's social-nutrition principle to the identified isolation (p. 410; inference).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 410, 428.
ref: Hazzard Ch 30 — NUTRITION DISORDERS, OBESITY , AND ENTERAL/PARENTERAL ALIMENTATION · Harrison Ch 50 — Unintentional Weight Loss
chapterTitle: NUTRITION DISORDERS, OBESITY , AND ENTERAL/PARENTERAL ALIMENTATION

q: A sedentary 77-year-old woman with osteoarthritis wants to begin exercising. Her medical condition has been assessed and is stable. Which principle should guide the initial program?
o: Start at full workload and reduce it when marked pain develops
Choose a fixed workload and maintain it after capacity improves
Start at low workload and progress with capacity and response
Choose vigorous sessions and avoid pauses for recovery during exercise
explanation:
**Exercise intensity and progression** should match the older adult's capacity. The source recommends starting at a lower level, supervising initial exercise, increasing goals as they are achieved, and allowing the longer recovery time older adults need (p. 824).
"Older adults who are beginning a program may need to start with 5 to 10 minutes of continuous activity at a lower intensity." (p. 824).
"Exercise should be supervised initially to assure appropriate changes in heart rate and blood pressure." (p. 824).

**A. Start at full workload and reduce it when marked pain develops.** Wrong, the recommended starting point is a lower workload, rather than waiting for marked pain after a full workload (p. 824).
**B. Choose a fixed workload and maintain it after capacity improves.** Wrong, exercise goals should increase after they are achieved, so a fixed load despite improvement misses progressive challenge (p. 824).
**C. Start at low workload and progress with capacity and response.** Correct, this matches the lower starting level and subsequent progression described (p. 824).
**D. Choose vigorous sessions and avoid pauses for recovery during exercise.** Wrong, older adults need longer recovery between bouts and sessions, not avoidance of recovery pauses (p. 824).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 824.

q: An 86-year-old man with moderate dementia, heart failure (EF 40%), and stage 4 CKD (eGFR 24; Cockcroft-Gault CrCl 22 mL/min) physically resists care and has thrown a cup at another resident. He takes donepezil 10 mg, carvedilol 6.25 mg twice daily, and furosemide 20 mg daily. After assessing contributors and trying nonpharmacologic measures, dangerous aggression persists. If the risk-benefit assessment favors risperidone, which prescribing approach matches Hazzard?
o: Start low, monitor adverse effects, and titrate to the effective dose
Start at a high dose, then reduce treatment when behavioral control is established
Start several psychotropic drugs together, then identify the most useful combination
Continue treatment without a stop plan, using sedation as the principal target
explanation:
**Antipsychotic treatment** in dementia requires a risk-benefit assessment because benefits are modest and adverse effects include increased mortality and cardiovascular or cerebrovascular events. When treatment is justified for severe dangerous symptoms, start low and titrate to the minimum effective dose with monitoring (p. 927).
"treatment should be initiated at a low dose and titrated to the minimum effective dose as tolerated." (p. 927).

**A. Start low, monitor adverse effects, and titrate to the effective dose.** Correct, This directly implements the source's dose and monitoring principles after the stated assessment (p. 927).
**B. Start at a high dose, then reduce treatment when behavioral control is established.** Wrong, Starting high conflicts with low-dose initiation and increases exposure without first establishing the minimum effective dose (p. 927; application).
**C. Start several psychotropic drugs together, then identify the most useful combination.** Wrong, The source recommends changing one medication at a time to clarify effects and reduce adverse effects (p. 927).
**D. Continue treatment without a stop plan, using sedation as the principal target.** Wrong, The source calls for defined targets and time-limited psychotropic use, with sedation monitored as an adverse effect rather than the principal goal (p. 927).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 927.
ref: Hazzard Ch 60 — BEHAVIORAL SYMPTOMS OF DEMENTIA AND PSYCHOACTIVE DRUG THERAPY· Harrison Ch 433 — Approach to the Patient with Neurologic Disease
chapterTitle: Behavioral Symptoms of Dementia and Psychoactive Drug Therapy

q: A 75-year-old woman with documented cognitive decline still bathes and dresses independently. The clinician is distinguishing mild cognitive impairment from early dementia. Which financial-management finding, if caused by her cognitive decline, indicates loss of the independence required for MCI?
o: Managing finances independently but taking longer than before
Needing help with finances because of repeated errors
Managing finances independently but less efficiently than before
Managing finances independently but making more errors than before
explanation:
**Preserved functional independence** is required for MCI. The criteria allow slower, less efficient, or more error-prone performance while independence is maintained; needing assistance crosses that functional distinction (p. 896; application).
"The patient maintains preserved independence in functional abilities, although they may take more time, be less efficient, and make more errors at performing such activities than in the past." (p. 896).

**A. Managing finances independently but taking longer than before.** Wrong, Taking more time while remaining independent is explicitly compatible with MCI (p. 896).
**B. Needing help with finances because of repeated errors.** Correct, Needing assistance represents loss of independence, unlike the other descriptions; this finding supports a dementia-level functional impact when due to cognitive decline (p. 896; inference).
**C. Managing finances independently but less efficiently than before.** Wrong, Reduced efficiency is allowed in MCI when functional independence is preserved (p. 896).
**D. Managing finances independently but making more errors than before.** Wrong, More errors can occur in MCI if the person still maintains independence; errors alone do not show the loss asked about (p. 896).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 896.
ref: Hazzard Ch 59 — DEMENTIA INCLUDING ALZHEIMER DISEASE · Harrison Ch 433 — Approach to the Patient with Neurologic Disease

q: An 83-year-old man with advanced COPD, FEV1 30% predicted, coronary disease, and frailty with CFS 6 is hospitalized with pneumonia. After 48 hours of antibiotics, he remains on 4 L of oxygen with little improvement. He has no advance directive. His daughter asks the team to do everything. Which approach best begins a goals-of-care discussion?
o: Recommend a DNR order from the disease severity before exploring his values
Recommend comfort-focused care before establishing what outcomes he values
Explore what doing everything means to the patient and family
Defer discussion of values while continuing the current treatment plan
explanation:
**Doing everything needs clarification.** Hazzard recommends understanding what this request means and considering whether interventions advance the patient’s goals (p. 1103). "When the goal is to do “everything,” medical teams may want to better understand what this means to a patient and family." (p. 1103).

**A. Recommend a DNR order from the disease severity before exploring his values.** Wrong, a recommendation made before exploring values omits the source’s requirement to understand preferences (p. 1103).
**B. Recommend comfort-focused care before establishing what outcomes he values.** Wrong, the source says recommendations should be based on the patient’s values and preferences, which have not yet been established (p. 1103).
**C. Explore what doing everything means to the patient and family.** Correct, this clarifies the meaning of the request before deciding which interventions fit the patient’s goals (p. 1103).
**D. Defer discussion of values while continuing the current treatment plan.** Wrong, postponement leaves the central request unexplored; the source recommends clarifying its meaning (p. 1103).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 1103.

q: An older woman with recurrent falls takes amitriptyline for neuropathic pain. Which adverse-effect profile supports reassessing this medicine under the 2023 AGS Beers Criteria?
o: Anticholinergic effects with sedation and orthostatic hypotension
Anticholinergic effects with alertness and improved postural stability
Sedative effects with protection against orthostatic blood-pressure changes
Antidepressant effects with alertness and improved postural stability
explanation:
**Amitriptyline** is included among antidepressants with strong anticholinergic activity. Their listed rationale for avoidance is "Highly anticholinergic, sedating, and cause orthostatic hypotension;" (p. 2059). Sedation and postural hypotension support reassessment in this fall-prone patient; this is an application of that adverse-effect profile, not a quantified comparison with other interventions.

**A. Anticholinergic effects with sedation and orthostatic hypotension.** Correct, this matches the anticholinergic, sedating and orthostatic effects given in the table (p. 2059).
**B. Anticholinergic effects with alertness and improved postural stability.** Wrong, the table describes sedation and orthostatic hypotension, not improved alertness and postural stability (p. 2059).
**C. Sedative effects with protection against orthostatic blood-pressure changes.** Wrong, sedation is recognized, but the drug causes orthostatic hypotension rather than protecting against it (p. 2059).
**D. Antidepressant effects with alertness and improved postural stability.** Wrong, classification as an antidepressant does not change the listed sedating and hypotensive effects; improved alertness and postural stability are not the profile given (p. 2059).

Source: 2023 AGS Beers Criteria, Table 2, pp. 2059.
ref: Hazzard Ch 43 — FALLS · Harrison Ch 26 — Neurologic Causes of Weakness and Paralysis

q: An 80-year-old man with mild Alzheimer dementia lives with his 82-year-old wife, who has severe arthritis. He has wandered outside twice this week. She manages their instrumental activities and appears exhausted. She says, "I promised we would never go to a nursing home." Which approach to discussing long-term services follows Hazzard?
o: Choose a home service from her stated preference before assessing their support needs
Choose a nursing facility from the dementia diagnosis before discussing service options
Explore their preferences and match available services to their assessed support needs
Choose a placement service from his wandering history before discussing their preferences
explanation:
**Long-term services** span different levels and settings of support (p. 240). Their use depends on "the fit between the needs of an older adult and the care model" and on the person's preferences and local availability (p. 240). Applied to this vignette, discussing all three is an inference from that selection principle, rather than assuming a placement decision from one feature.

**A. Choose a home service from her stated preference before assessing their support needs.** Wrong, Preference matters, but selecting a service before assessing needs omits the required fit between needs and care model (p. 240).
**B. Choose a nursing facility from the dementia diagnosis before discussing service options.** Wrong, Diagnosis by itself does not implement the source's needs, preferences, and availability framework (p. 240).
**C. Explore their preferences and match available services to their assessed support needs.** Correct, This considers the factors the source identifies for choosing among care models; applying that framework here is a clinical inference (p. 240).
**D. Choose a placement service from his wandering history before discussing their preferences.** Wrong, A decision based on wandering before exploring preferences omits one of the source's explicit selection factors (p. 240).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 240.
ref: Hazzard Ch 17 — COMMUNITY-BASED LONG-TERM SERVICES AND SUPPORT, AND HOME-BASED MEDICAL CARE
chapterTitle: COMMUNITY-BASED LONG-TERM SERVICES AND SUPPORT, AND HOME-BASED MEDICAL CARE

q: A 78-year-old woman takes nitrofurantoin daily for long-term suppression of recurrent urinary tract infections. Her creatinine clearance is 42 mL/min. According to the 2023 AGS Beers Criteria, which recommendation addresses the long-term suppression?
o: Stop long-term suppression and reassess the prevention plan
Continue long-term suppression with periodic renal-function monitoring
Reduce the daily dose and continue long-term suppression
Give the dose in the evening and continue long-term suppression
explanation:
**Long-term nitrofurantoin suppression** is discouraged because of pulmonary toxicity, hepatotoxicity, and peripheral neuropathy. The Beers recommendation to avoid prolonged suppression is separate from the creatinine-clearance restriction (p. 2057).
"Avoid in individuals with CrCl <30 mL/ min or for long-term suppression." (p. 2057).

**A. Stop long-term suppression and reassess the prevention plan.** Correct, this addresses the recommendation to avoid long-term suppression (p. 2057).
**B. Continue long-term suppression with periodic renal-function monitoring.** Wrong, renal monitoring does not remove the separate recommendation against long-term suppression (p. 2057).
**C. Reduce the daily dose and continue long-term suppression.** Wrong, lowering the dose does not address the recommendation to avoid the prolonged suppressive course (p. 2057).
**D. Give the dose in the evening and continue long-term suppression.** Wrong, changing the time of administration does not address the risk of long-term use (p. 2057).

Source: 2023 AGS Beers Criteria, pp. 2057.
ref: Hazzard Ch 22 — MEDICATION PRESCRIBING AND DE-PRESCRIBING

q: An 85-year-old man develops delirium with inattention and disorganized thinking over one day. He has no fever, head trauma, focal neurologic deficit, or suspected seizure. The initial assessment has not found a cause, but medication review remains incomplete: his daughter provides a partial list including an unidentified sleep preparation. What should be completed next?
o: Obtain brain CT as the next component of the initial evaluation
Perform lumbar puncture and cerebrospinal fluid testing next
Complete review of prescribed and nonprescription medications
Obtain EEG as the next component of the initial evaluation
explanation:
**Medication review and focused testing** are central to delirium evaluation. Hazzard states, “A complete medication review, including over-the-counter medications, is critical” (p. 885). Lumbar puncture, neuroimaging, and EEG are selected according to clinical clues rather than substituting for that initial evaluation (p. 885).

**A. Obtain brain CT as the next component of the initial evaluation.** Wrong, imaging can be appropriate when no cause is identifiable, but a critical part of this initial assessment remains unfinished (p. 885).
**B. Perform lumbar puncture and cerebrospinal fluid testing next.** Wrong, the source’s indication is fever with suspected meningitis or encephalitis, which the stem does not suggest (p. 885).
**C. Complete review of prescribed and nonprescription medications.** Correct, the unknown sleep preparation and incomplete list identify the required full medication review as the immediate unfinished task (p. 885).
**D. Obtain EEG as the next component of the initial evaluation.** Wrong, EEG for subclinical seizures or selected differentiation from psychiatric illness does not displace the incomplete medication review here (p. 885).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 885.
label: Source: Hazzard 8e (marked) · p.885

q: A 74-year-old woman with diabetes and HbA1c 7.2% reports dizziness and near-falls. She takes metformin 1000 mg twice daily, glipizide 5 mg daily, and lisinopril 10 mg daily, and recently began tramadol 50 mg three times daily for osteoarthritis pain. Pre-lunch glucose values are 68–75 mg/dL. When reviewing glipizide because of concern about hypoglycemia, which statement follows Hazzard?
o: Withdraw glipizide because sulfonylureas should be avoided when hypoglycemia is a concern
Continue glipizide because pancreatic insulin release is not part of its mechanism of action
Continue glipizide because hypoglycemia is not an adverse effect of its drug class
Substitute glyburide because its longer half-life lowers hypoglycemia risk in older people
explanation:
**Sulfonylureas** enhance pancreatic insulin secretion, and hypoglycemia is their main adverse effect. Although glipizide may be safer than glyburide in older people, the chapter advises avoiding the class when there is concern about hypoglycemia (p. 1579).
"Their primary mechanism of action is to enhance insulin secretion by the β-cells of the endocrine pancreas." (p. 1579).
"Sulfonylurea drugs have established a long record of safety, with hypoglycemia being the main adverse effect." (p. 1579).

**A. Withdraw glipizide because sulfonylureas should be avoided when hypoglycemia is a concern.** Correct, this applies the source's class-level advice to the glucose concern in the stem without attributing every symptom to one drug (p. 1579).
**B. Continue glipizide because pancreatic insulin release is not part of its mechanism of action.** Wrong, enhancing insulin secretion by pancreatic beta cells is the stated primary mechanism of sulfonylureas (p. 1579).
**C. Continue glipizide because hypoglycemia is not an adverse effect of its drug class.** Wrong, hypoglycemia is explicitly the main adverse effect of this class (p. 1579).
**D. Substitute glyburide because its longer half-life lowers hypoglycemia risk in older people.** Wrong, glyburide's long half-life is associated with higher, not lower, hypoglycemia risk in older patients (p. 1579).

Source: Hazzard’s Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8e, pp. 1579.
ref: Hazzard Ch 99 — DIABETES MELLITUS · Harrison Ch 388 — Approach to the Patient with Endocrine Disorders

q: אישה הוגדרה כחולה הנוטה למות שאינה בעלת כשרות. אין הנחיות מקדימות, ייפוי כוח או החלטת ועדה, ובני המשפחה חלוקים בנוגע להזנה מלאכותית. איזה מידע רלוונטי לרופא האחראי בבירור רצונה לפי סעיף 5?
o: העדפת הבן לפי מיקומו בסדר הלידה במשפחה
העדפת רוב בני המשפחה לפי הצבעה ביניהם
הצהרה מפורשת של אדם קרוב על רצונה שלה
העדפת בן המשפחה שמבקר בתדירות הגבוהה ביותר
explanation:
בירור **רצון החולה** מתמקד במה שהחולה רצתה, ולא בהעדפות קרוביה עבור עצמם. בהעדר המסלולים המנויים בחוק, הרופא האחראי מתחשב בהצהרה מפורשת של אדם קרוב על רצונה; זהו רכיב בבירור ולא הכרעה אוטומטית בעד הזנה או נגדה (עמ׳ 5–6, סעיף 5).
"על פי החלטת רופא אחראי ובתנאי שההחלטה כאמור תתקבל בהתחשב" (עמ׳ 6).
"בהצהרה מפורשת של אדם קרוב ולפיה החולה הנוטה למות אינו רוצה להוסיף לחיות;" (עמ׳ 6).

**א. העדפת הבן לפי מיקומו בסדר הלידה במשפחה.** שגויה, סדר לידה אינו הקריטריון שבסעיף; נדרש מידע על רצון החולה (עמ׳ 6).
**ב. העדפת רוב בני המשפחה לפי הצבעה ביניהם.** שגויה, הסעיף אינו קובע הצבעת משפחה אלא התחשבות בהצהרה הנוגעת לרצונה של החולה (עמ׳ 6).
**ג. הצהרה מפורשת של אדם קרוב על רצונה שלה.** נכונה, זהו סוג המידע המנוי במפורש לשיקול הרופא האחראי בתנאים המתוארים (עמ׳ 6).
**ד. העדפת בן המשפחה שמבקר בתדירות הגבוהה ביותר.** שגויה, תדירות ביקורים כשלעצמה אינה מחליפה הצהרה בדבר רצון החולה (עמ׳ 6).

מקור: חוק החולה הנוטה למות, תשס_ו-2005.pdf, עמ׳ 6.
ref: Hazzard Ch 72 — ETHICAL ISSUES· Harrison Ch 433 — Approach to the Patient with Neurologic Disease

q: A 79-year-old man awaiting a below-knee amputation asks about returning to mobility with a prosthesis. Which functional assessment supports rehabilitation planning according to Hazzard?
o: Assess potential from arm strength and chronological age
Assess previous walking, medical status, and ability to learn
Assess potential from kidney disease stage and chronological age
Assess potential from diabetes duration and the prosthesis type
explanation:
**Post-amputation functional potential** depends on prior function, ability to meet the physiological demands of prosthetic use, and ability to learn new skills. Hazzard uses these considerations to develop rehabilitation goals rather than inferring potential from age or a single disease descriptor (p. 831). "Considerations in determining the potential functional status of someone after an amputation may include prior ability to walk," (p. 831).

**A. Assess potential from arm strength and chronological age.** Wrong, arm strength and age omit prior walking ability and the broader medical and learning assessment specified (p. 831).
**B. Assess previous walking, medical status, and ability to learn.** Correct, these are the three domains explicitly listed for estimating potential functional status (p. 831).
**C. Assess potential from kidney disease stage and chronological age.** Wrong, kidney disease belongs in medical assessment but does not replace prior walking ability or capacity to learn (p. 831).
**D. Assess potential from diabetes duration and the prosthesis type.** Wrong, disease duration and a device label do not supply the required assessment of function, medical demands, and learning (p. 831).

Source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th ed., pp. 831.

q: An 84-year-old man with renal impairment, reduced fluid intake, and mild dementia develops delirium. He takes morphine and gabapentin and now has hypotension and worsening kidney function. Which approach addresses potentially treatable contributors?
o: Review medication while evaluating acute illness and fluid status
Reduce one medication and defer other evaluation pending the response
Start sedation and defer evaluation of the physical changes
Attribute the change to dementia and repeat cognitive testing later
explanation:
**Delirium often has multiple contributors**, so evaluation should combine examination, medication review, and investigations guided by the presentation. "Identifying the potentially multifactorial contributors to the delirium is of paramount importance." (p. 885). The source also states, "A complete medication review, including over-the-counter medications, is critical." (p. 885).

**A. Review medication while evaluating acute illness and fluid status.** Correct, this evaluates medication exposure alongside the new physical abnormalities, applying the source’s multifactorial approach (p. 885).
**B. Reduce one medication and defer other evaluation pending the response.** Wrong, waiting after one drug change delays the broader evaluation needed to identify other treatable contributors (p. 885).
**C. Start sedation and defer evaluation of the physical changes.** Wrong, symptom sedation does not establish the cause of the new hypotension and renal deterioration; those findings warrant medical evaluation (p. 885).
**D. Attribute the change to dementia and repeat cognitive testing later.** Wrong, the acute change requires evaluation for delirium and new illness rather than attribution to baseline dementia (p. 885).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 885.
ref: Hazzard Ch 22 — MEDICATION PRESCRIBING AND DE-PRESCRIBING

q: A 79-year-old woman is brought by her daughter for routine follow-up. She has fallen twice in the past month and seems more forgetful. She lives alone and manages her finances, but recently burned a pot while cooking. She takes donepezil 10 mg daily, amitriptyline 50 mg at night for neuropathic pain, lisinopril 10 mg daily, and atorvastatin 40 mg daily. Blood pressure is 128/78 sitting and 108/65 after three minutes standing. Her Mini-Cog score is 2/5. Which approach to amitriptyline addresses the medication concern identified in Beers 2023?
o: Retain amitriptyline because it has little effect on standing blood pressure
Review amitriptyline for discontinuation because of anticholinergic and orthostatic effects
Increase amitriptyline because stronger anticholinergic activity supports cognitive function
Replace amitriptyline with imipramine to avoid the strongly anticholinergic antidepressant group
explanation:
**Amitriptyline** is strongly anticholinergic and sedating and can cause orthostatic hypotension. Beers recommends avoiding this antidepressant group, which also includes imipramine (p. 2059).
"Highly anticholinergic, sedating, and cause orthostatic hypotension;" (p. 2059).
"Antidepressants with strong anticholinergic activity, alone or in combination" (p. 2059).

**A. Retain amitriptyline because it has little effect on standing blood pressure.** Wrong, orthostatic hypotension is explicitly part of the rationale for avoiding the drug group (p. 2059).
**B. Review amitriptyline for discontinuation because of anticholinergic and orthostatic effects.** Correct, it addresses the properties identified by the criterion without claiming a proven ranking of fall-prevention interventions (p. 2059; application).
**C. Increase amitriptyline because stronger anticholinergic activity supports cognitive function.** Wrong, strong anticholinergic activity is a reason for avoidance, not a rationale for increasing treatment to support cognition (p. 2059).
**D. Replace amitriptyline with imipramine to avoid the strongly anticholinergic antidepressant group.** Wrong, imipramine is in the same group, so the substitution does not avoid strongly anticholinergic antidepressants (p. 2059).

Source: 2023 AGS Beers Criteria, pp. 2059.
ref: Hazzard Ch 22 — MEDICATION PRESCRIBING AND DE-PRESCRIBING

q: בישראל, חולה שנקבע לגביו שהוא נוטה למות כבר קיבל החלטה על היקף הטיפול הרצוי לו. במהלך האשפוז משתנים מצבו הנשימתי ורצונו ביחס לטיפול. מה נדרש מהרופא האחראי לפי החוק?
o: להותיר את התוכנית הקודמת עד שיסתיים האשפוז הנוכחי
להעריך את השינוי ולחזור ולהחליט על דרך הטיפול
להסתמך על ההחלטה הראשונה עד לביקורת במרפאה
להעביר את ההחלטה לצוות הבא בלי הערכה מחודשת
explanation:
**הערכה חוזרת** היא חובה מפורשת בחוק החולה הנוטה למות. שינוי במצב הרפואי או ברצון מחייב את הרופא האחראי לחזור להחלטה על דרך הטיפול, ולא להסתפק בתוכנית קודמת (סעיף 12, עמ׳ 8).
"על הרופא האחראי להעריך, מדי פעם, את כשרותו, מצבו הרפואי ואת רצונו של החולה הנוטה למות;" (עמ׳ 8).
"חל שינוי באחד מאלה – עליו לחזור ולהחליט לענין דרך הטיפול הרפואי בו." (עמ׳ 8).

**א. להותיר את התוכנית הקודמת עד שיסתיים האשפוז הנוכחי.** שגויה, שינוי במצב או ברצון מחייב בחינה מחודשת כבר כעת ולא בסיום האשפוז (עמ׳ 8).
**ב. להעריך את השינוי ולחזור ולהחליט על דרך הטיפול.** נכונה, האפשרות ממלאת את חובת ההערכה וההחלטה החוזרת (עמ׳ 8).
**ג. להסתמך על ההחלטה הראשונה עד לביקורת במרפאה.** שגויה, תוכנית קודמת אינה פוטרת מהערכה מחדש כשחל שינוי (עמ׳ 8).
**ד. להעביר את ההחלטה לצוות הבא בלי הערכה מחודשת.** שגויה, החובה חלה על הרופא האחראי; העברה בלי הערכה אינה מקיימת אותה (עמ׳ 8).

מקור: חוק החולה הנוטה למות, עמ׳ 8.
ref: Hazzard Ch 7 — DECISION MAKING AND ADVANCE CARE PLANNING: WHAT MATTERS MOST
chapterTitle: DECISION MAKING AND ADVANCE CARE PLANNING: WHAT MATTERS MOST

q: A woman taking metformin is hospitalized with a severe acute illness that reduces tissue perfusion. Which risk explains avoiding metformin in this setting?
o: Lactic acidosis in the setting of reduced tissue perfusion
Excess insulin in the setting of pancreatic stimulation
Metabolic alkalosis in the setting of increased acid loss
Fluid overload in the setting of increased sodium retention
explanation:
**Lactic acidosis** is the complication underlying this precaution. Although rare with metformin, it is the stated concern during major acute illness with impaired tissue perfusion (p. 1576). The source identifies "decreased tissue perfusion as a precipitating factor for lactic acidosis." (p. 1576).

**A. Lactic acidosis in the setting of reduced tissue perfusion.** Correct, the source explicitly connects reduced perfusion during major illness with the lactic-acidosis risk underlying avoidance of metformin (p. 1576).
**B. Excess insulin in the setting of pancreatic stimulation.** Wrong, the precaution asked about concerns lactic acidosis with impaired perfusion, rather than excess insulin from pancreatic stimulation (p. 1576).
**C. Metabolic alkalosis in the setting of increased acid loss.** Wrong, the source identifies lactic acidosis, rather than alkalosis from acid loss, as the complication relevant to this setting (p. 1576).
**D. Fluid overload in the setting of increased sodium retention.** Wrong, sodium retention is not the risk on which this stated metformin precaution is based; the source specifies lactic acidosis (p. 1576).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 1576.
ref: Hazzard Ch 22 — MEDICATION PRESCRIBING AND DE-PRESCRIBING

q: An 82-year-old man recently returned from rehabilitation after a hip fracture. His daughter reports that he sleeps 14 hours daily, eats little, and no longer reads the newspaper. Medicines added during admission were oxycodone 5 mg every six hours as needed, quetiapine 25 mg at night for sleep, pantoprazole 40 mg daily, and docusate 100 mg twice daily. Before the fracture he was independent in all instrumental activities of daily living; his current IADL score is 3/8. Which approach to the quetiapine insomnia prescription follows Hazzard?
o: Continue quetiapine because trials establish its routine benefit for insomnia
Increase quetiapine because sedation establishes its safety for older adults
Review quetiapine for discontinuation because routine insomnia use is discouraged
Replace quetiapine with diphenhydramine as the primary treatment for chronic insomnia
explanation:
**Sedating antipsychotics** have scant evidence of efficacy for insomnia and can cause significant adverse events. Hazzard discourages their routine use for insomnia without a serious psychiatric indication and also advises against diphenhydramine as primary insomnia treatment (p. 661).
"there is scant evidence demonstrating their efficacy, and these medications can have significant adverse events," (p. 661).
"sedating antipsychotics should not routinely be used in the management of insomnia in older adults without coexisting serious psychiatric conditions that warrant use of these agents." (p. 661).

**A. Continue quetiapine because trials establish its routine benefit for insomnia.** Wrong, evidence of efficacy is described as scant, so the stated reason for routine continuation is unsupported (p. 661).
**B. Increase quetiapine because sedation establishes its safety for older adults.** Wrong, sedation does not establish safety; the source warns of significant adverse events (p. 661).
**C. Review quetiapine for discontinuation because routine insomnia use is discouraged.** Correct, it prompts reassessment of an antipsychotic prescribed for sleep without predicting the magnitude of functional recovery (p. 661; application).
**D. Replace quetiapine with diphenhydramine as the primary treatment for chronic insomnia.** Wrong, diphenhydramine is specifically discouraged as primary insomnia treatment in older patients (p. 661).

Source: Hazzard’s Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8e, pp. 661.
ref: Hazzard Ch 22 — MEDICATION PRESCRIBING AND DE-PRESCRIBING

q: A 91-year-old woman with vascular dementia and chronic kidney disease develops acute confusion in assisted living. Evaluation finds no urinary symptoms, fever, or hemodynamic instability. Urinalysis shows pyuria and a few bacteria, and nitrofurantoin was started for suspected UTI. Which approach follows the source’s advice about nonspecific symptoms without localizing evidence of UTI?
o: Continue nitrofurantoin and add medication for agitation
Replace nitrofurantoin with a broader-spectrum antibiotic
Stop nitrofurantoin, monitor, and evaluate other causes
Continue nitrofurantoin while awaiting a urine culture
explanation:
**Confusion and abnormal urine findings do not by themselves establish symptomatic UTI.** Hazzard states that "unless more specific localizing signs and symptoms for UTI are present, clinicians should NOT initiate UTI treatment for these symptoms." (p. 1703). Monitoring should accompany evaluation for other causes of the acute change (pp. 885, 1703).

**A. Continue nitrofurantoin and add medication for agitation.** Wrong, continuing antibiotic treatment lacks the localizing evidence required by the source; treating agitation does not resolve that diagnostic gap (pp. 885, 1703).
**B. Replace nitrofurantoin with a broader-spectrum antibiotic.** Wrong, broadening antibiotics does not supply evidence that the urinary tract is the cause of the confusion (p. 1703).
**C. Stop nitrofurantoin, monitor, and evaluate other causes.** Correct, this applies the no-treatment principle to an antibiotic already started without supporting symptoms, while continuing assessment and observation (pp. 885, 1703; clinical application).
**D. Continue nitrofurantoin while awaiting a urine culture.** Wrong, waiting for a culture does not justify continuing treatment for nonspecific confusion without localizing urinary symptoms (p. 1703).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 885, 1703.
ref: Hazzard Ch 22 — MEDICATION PRESCRIBING AND DE-PRESCRIBING

q: A 78-year-old man with Parkinson disease takes two hours to finish his morning routine, has difficulty fastening buttons, and walks with a shuffling gait. His MMSE is 24 and he pauses before answering. He also reports constipation and blurred vision. His drugs are carbidopa–levodopa 25/100 mg three times daily, ropinirole 2 mg three times daily, trihexyphenidyl 2 mg twice daily, and trazodone 50 mg at night. Which change addresses the antimuscarinic exposure that Hazzard advises avoiding at his age?
o: Increase levodopa while continuing trihexyphenidyl
Add rivastigmine while continuing trihexyphenidyl
Discontinue trihexyphenidyl during medication review
Increase ropinirole while continuing trihexyphenidyl
explanation:
**Antimuscarinic exposure** deserves review in an older person with Parkinson disease and cognitive symptoms. Hazzard lists trihexyphenidyl as an antimuscarinic and links this class to cognitive impairment and hallucinations (pp. 946–947). "For this reason, antimuscarinics should be avoided in patients older than 70 years." (p. 947).

**A. Increase levodopa while continuing trihexyphenidyl.** Wrong, this leaves the antimuscarinic exposure that the source advises avoiding (p. 947).
**B. Add rivastigmine while continuing trihexyphenidyl.** Wrong, adding a cognitive drug leaves the implicated antimuscarinic exposure in place (p. 947).
**C. Discontinue trihexyphenidyl during medication review.** Correct, this removes the listed antimuscarinic rather than adding another drug while retaining it (p. 947).
**D. Increase ropinirole while continuing trihexyphenidyl.** Wrong, this leaves trihexyphenidyl in place and therefore does not address the specified medication concern (p. 947).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 947.
ref: Hazzard Ch 61 — PARKINSON DISEASE AND RELATED DISORDERS · Harrison Ch 433 — Approach to the Patient with Neurologic Disease

q: An 86-year-old woman with heart failure and congestion is receiving a loop diuretic. After treatment adjustment her congestion improves and creatinine rises slightly. Which monitoring principle follows Hazzard?
o: Reduce diuresis for the creatinine rise despite persistent congestion
Assess volume status and electrolytes alongside the creatinine change
Use the creatinine change as the measure of fluid removal
Add metolazone to reduce the need for electrolyte monitoring
explanation:
**Creatinine changes must be interpreted with volume status.** Diuresis can resolve hemodilution and raise measured creatinine, while overdiuresis can also cause kidney injury; the rise therefore needs clinical interpretation (p. 1182). "For this reason, electrolytes should be monitored closely when diuretic therapy is being adjusted." (p. 1182).

**A. Reduce diuresis for the creatinine rise despite persistent congestion.** Wrong, the source warns that accepting persistent congestion to avoid titration can worsen symptoms and other outcomes; a creatinine rise alone does not settle the volume assessment (p. 1182).
**B. Assess volume status and electrolytes alongside the creatinine change.** Correct, this incorporates congestion, possible hypovolemia, and electrolyte effects into interpretation of creatinine (p. 1182).
**C. Use the creatinine change as the measure of fluid removal.** Wrong, the source describes a complex relationship influenced by hemodilution and perfusion, not a direct fluid-removal measurement (p. 1182).
**D. Add metolazone to reduce the need for electrolyte monitoring.** Wrong, metolazone requires particular monitoring because it can cause a brisk response and serious electrolyte disturbances (p. 1182).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 1182.

q: A medication review after a fall identifies zolpidem use for sleep in an older adult. How do the 2023 Beers Criteria characterize the balance of benefit and harm for Z-drugs?
o: Substantial sleep improvement with fewer delirium and fall events than benzodiazepines
Substantial sleep improvement with less cognitive impairment than benzodiazepines
Minimal sleep improvement with adverse events similar to benzodiazepines
Minimal sleep improvement with increased risk attributed chiefly to benzodiazepines
explanation:
**Z-drugs** provide minimal improvement in sleep latency and duration in older adults. The Beers Criteria describe adverse events similar to benzodiazepines, including delirium, falls, and fractures, and recommend avoidance (p. 2060). "minimal improvement in sleep latency and duration." (p. 2060).

**A. Substantial sleep improvement with fewer delirium and fall events than benzodiazepines.** Wrong, the source describes minimal sleep benefit and similar adverse events, not substantial benefit with fewer falls or delirium (p. 2060).
**B. Substantial sleep improvement with less cognitive impairment than benzodiazepines.** Wrong, the source does not support the proposed benefit or cognitive safety advantage; it describes minimal benefit and similar adverse events (p. 2060).
**C. Minimal sleep improvement with adverse events similar to benzodiazepines.** Correct, this matches both the limited sleep benefit and the benzodiazepine-like adverse-event profile (p. 2060).
**D. Minimal sleep improvement with increased risk attributed chiefly to benzodiazepines.** Wrong, the adverse events apply to Z-drugs themselves, rather than being confined chiefly to the comparison class (p. 2060).

Source: AGS Beers Criteria 2023, pp. 2060.

q: An older woman with hypernatremia and water deficit cannot drink safely. She also has intravascular volume depletion that threatens cardiovascular stability. What sequence of fluid treatment matches Hazzard?
o: Replace free water intravenously before restoring intravascular volume
Give oral water replacement before restoring intravascular volume
Withhold fluid replacement until the serum sodium has normalized
Restore intravascular volume with saline before using hypotonic fluid
explanation:
**Intravascular volume restoration** takes priority when cardiovascular status is threatened. "If the cardiovascular status is in jeopardy, then the initial fluid of choice is 0.9% saline to ensure adequate intravascular volume." (p. 588). After volume is established, a more hypotonic fluid addresses the water deficit, with sodium monitoring (p. 588).

**A. Replace free water intravenously before restoring intravascular volume.** Wrong, this places free-water replacement before the saline volume restoration specified when cardiovascular stability is threatened (p. 588).
**B. Give oral water replacement before restoring intravascular volume.** Wrong, the patient cannot drink safely, and the threatened circulation requires initial saline volume restoration (p. 588).
**C. Withhold fluid replacement until the serum sodium has normalized.** Wrong, fluid replacement is the treatment described for the deficit; waiting for sodium to normalize leaves the volume deficit untreated (p. 588).
**D. Restore intravascular volume with saline before using hypotonic fluid.** Correct, this follows the stated sequence: initial saline for cardiovascular compromise, then more hypotonic fluid once volume is established (p. 588).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 588.
ref: Hazzard Ch 22 — MEDICATION PRESCRIBING AND DE-PRESCRIBING

q: A 79-year-old woman with mild dementia and pneumonia develops delirium after receiving diphenhydramine for sleep. What should the medication assessment consider?
o: A medication effect that protects against confusion during infection
A medication contribution alongside the effects of the infection
A medication effect that excludes infection as a contributor
A medication effect that establishes progression of dementia
explanation:
**Diphenhydramine can contribute to delirium.** Hazzard lists delirium and reduced cognition among its adverse effects and advises against using it as primary insomnia treatment in older patients (p. 661). "Patients may also experience dry mouth, urinary retention, delirium, decreased cognition, constipation, and increased ocular pressure." (p. 661). Delirium assessment should consider potentially multiple contributors (p. 885).

**A. A medication effect that protects against confusion during infection.** Wrong, the cited adverse-effect list includes delirium, rather than protection from confusion (p. 661).
**B. A medication contribution alongside the effects of the infection.** Correct, the medication is a plausible additional contributor and does not replace evaluation of the intercurrent illness (pp. 661, 885).
**C. A medication effect that excludes infection as a contributor.** Wrong, delirium may have multiple contributors, so a possible drug effect does not exclude infection (p. 885).
**D. A medication effect that establishes progression of dementia.** Wrong, a recognized acute adverse drug effect does not establish dementia progression; the source distinguishes acute delirium from more insidious dementia (pp. 661, 885).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 661, 885.

q: An 81-year-old man with Parkinson disease develops confusion and visual hallucinations after amantadine is added. Which benefit-risk pairing explains why the treatment should be reassessed?
o: Reduced dyskinesia with a tendency to block dopaminergic activity
Reduced dyskinesia with a tendency to improve visual hallucinations
Reduced dyskinesia with a risk of confusion and hallucinations
Reduced dyskinesia with a tendency to decrease ankle edema
explanation:
**Amantadine** can reduce levodopa-induced dyskinesias through its antiglutamatergic action. The source also lists confusion and visual hallucinations as adverse effects, matching the new findings in this patient (p. 944).
"Its antiglutamatergic action is useful in reducing the severity of levodopa-induced dyskinesias" (p. 944).
"it can induce livedo reticularis, ankle edema, visual hallucinations, and confusion." (p. 944).

**A. Reduced dyskinesia with a tendency to block dopaminergic activity.** Wrong, the source describes stimulation of dopamine release and blockade of dopamine uptake, rather than blockade of dopaminergic activity (p. 944).
**B. Reduced dyskinesia with a tendency to improve visual hallucinations.** Wrong, visual hallucinations are a potential adverse effect, not the proposed accompanying benefit (p. 944).
**C. Reduced dyskinesia with a risk of confusion and hallucinations.** Correct, this combines the described antidyskinetic benefit with the adverse effects that prompted reassessment (p. 944).
**D. Reduced dyskinesia with a tendency to decrease ankle edema.** Wrong, ankle edema is a potential adverse effect, so reduction of edema is not the accompanying effect described by the source (p. 944).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 944.
ref: Hazzard Ch 61 — PARKINSON DISEASE AND RELATED DISORDERS · Harrison Ch 433 — Approach to the Patient with Neurologic Disease

q: An 88-year-old woman with advanced COPD is seen in palliative care. She uses continuous oxygen and a wheelchair and needs assistance with all activities of daily living. Because of treatment burden, she asks to stop her medications, including prednisone taken daily for two years. What approach applies if chronic prednisone is discontinued?
o: Stop prednisone and monitor for recurrent respiratory symptoms
Stop prednisone and restart it if fatigue develops
Taper prednisone gradually to allow adrenal-axis recovery
Stop prednisone and reserve replacement for a future illness
explanation:
**Chronic corticosteroid withdrawal** requires a taper because the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis needs time to recover. The source states that tapering is necessary "in order to allow the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis to recover and to avoid adrenal crisis." (p. 1532).

**A. Stop prednisone and monitor for recurrent respiratory symptoms.** Wrong, waiting for respiratory symptoms after abrupt withdrawal does not implement the taper required to permit adrenal-axis recovery (p. 1532).
**B. Stop prednisone and restart it if fatigue develops.** Wrong, waiting for fatigue after abrupt withdrawal does not prevent the adrenal-crisis risk for which a taper is recommended (p. 1532).
**C. Taper prednisone gradually to allow adrenal-axis recovery.** Correct, this follows the stated reason for tapering chronic corticosteroids rather than abruptly withdrawing them (p. 1532).
**D. Stop prednisone and reserve replacement for a future illness.** Wrong, a plan for future illness does not replace the taper needed during current discontinuation of chronic corticosteroid therapy (p. 1532).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 1532.
ref: Hazzard Ch 22 — MEDICATION PRESCRIBING AND DE-PRESCRIBING

q: During medication review for an older adult with recurrent hypoglycemia, which glucose-lowering drug class does Hazzard advise avoiding when hypoglycemia is a concern?
o: Treatment with DPP-4 inhibitors.
Treatment with sulfonylurea drugs.
Treatment with SGLT2 inhibitors.
Treatment with GLP-1 agonists.
explanation:
**Sulfonylureas** enhance insulin secretion and have hypoglycemia as their main adverse effect (p. 1579). Hazzard states that glipizide may be safer in older patients than other drugs in the class but still advises avoiding the class when hypoglycemia is a concern. "Glipizide may be safer to use in older patients, but all of these drugs should be avoided if there is concern about hypoglycemia." (p. 1579).

**A. Treatment with DPP-4 inhibitors.** Wrong, DPP-4 inhibitors rarely cause hypoglycemia when used alone: their incretin-mediated effect on insulin secretion decreases as glucose falls. That description does not match the class-specific avoidance statement asked about here (p. 1579).
**B. Treatment with sulfonylurea drugs.** Correct, the source’s avoidance statement applies to sulfonylureas, including glipizide, when hypoglycemia is a concern. Their insulin-secretory action and hypoglycemia adverse effect directly address the problem in the stem (p. 1579).
**C. Treatment with SGLT2 inhibitors.** Wrong, SGLT2 inhibitors are described as rarely causing hypoglycemia and lower glucose by increasing urinary glucose excretion. They are not the class targeted by the source’s sulfonylurea avoidance statement (p. 1580).
**D. Treatment with GLP-1 agonists.** Wrong, GLP-1 agonists enhance glucose-dependent insulin secretion and are described as rarely causing hypoglycemia. That is different from the sulfonylurea warning being tested (p. 1580).

Source: Hazzard’s Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th ed., pp. 1579, 1580.

q: An 85-year-old woman living independently has stopped hosting family meals and needs help with shopping, cooking, and medication management. Cognitive testing shows recall and clock-drawing difficulties. Examination and laboratory results are normal, and MRI shows mild atrophy. Donepezil has been started. Which additional approach directly evaluates her daily care needs and home safety?
o: Use medication-dose escalation in place of evaluating daily task performance
Arrange an in-home occupational therapy assessment to guide practical support
Use the cognitive screening score in place of evaluating daily task performance
Use the degree of MRI atrophy in place of evaluating daily task performance
explanation:
**In-home occupational therapy** can assess functional care needs and the safety of the home environment (p. 925). The source recommends an environment that supports remaining abilities and daily activities, rather than inferring care needs from a single test (p. 924). Such assessments "can provide useful data about a patient’s care needs" (p. 925).

**A. Use medication-dose escalation in place of evaluating daily task performance.** Wrong, A dose change does not perform the functional and home-safety assessment that the source recommends for these daily difficulties (pp. 924–925).
**B. Arrange an in-home occupational therapy assessment to guide practical support.** Correct, The assessment directly examines the care needs and home safety relevant to the cooking and medication-management difficulties (p. 925).
**C. Use the cognitive screening score in place of evaluating daily task performance.** Wrong, A cognitive score is not the in-home functional assessment described for determining task-related care needs and safety (p. 925).
**D. Use the degree of MRI atrophy in place of evaluating daily task performance.** Wrong, The cited approach evaluates function and environment; MRI atrophy does not substitute for assessing those practical needs (pp. 924–925).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 924, 925.
ref: Hazzard Ch 59 — DEMENTIA INCLUDING ALZHEIMER DISEASE

q: An 87-year-old man with mild cognitive impairment (MoCA 22/30) and hypertension is seen in the emergency department after a fall at his assisted-living facility. His daughter reports two other falls during the past month. He takes amlodipine 10 mg daily, donepezil 10 mg daily, and trazodone 50 mg at bedtime. Blood pressure is 138/82 sitting and 118/70 after three minutes standing. Cockcroft-Gault creatinine clearance is 42 mL/min. Which approach to his insomnia treatment is consistent with Hazzard?
o: Review trazodone and introduce a behavioral insomnia treatment plan
Increase trazodone because it improves orthostatic blood-pressure control
Replace trazodone with diphenhydramine as primary treatment for chronic insomnia
Retain trazodone because sustained benefit is established in nondepressed patients
explanation:
**Trazodone** is associated with daytime sleepiness and orthostatic hypotension, and its evidence for insomnia without depression is limited. Behavioral insomnia treatment is first-line therapy; these statements support reviewing trazodone rather than predicting a uniquely largest reduction in falls (p. 661).
"Trazadone has been associated with daytime sleepiness, headache, and orthostatic hypotension as well as priapism." (p. 661).
"It is the recommended first-line treatment for insomnia in all adults." (p. 661).

**A. Review trazodone and introduce a behavioral insomnia treatment plan.** Correct, it addresses the drug's relevant adverse effects while using the source-recommended behavioral treatment approach (p. 661; application).
**B. Increase trazodone because it improves orthostatic blood-pressure control.** Wrong, orthostatic hypotension is a reported adverse effect, not a condition that trazodone is described as improving (p. 661).
**C. Replace trazodone with diphenhydramine as primary treatment for chronic insomnia.** Wrong, diphenhydramine is specifically discouraged as primary insomnia treatment in older patients (p. 661).
**D. Retain trazodone because sustained benefit is established in nondepressed patients.** Wrong, in the cited study of nondepressed patients, short-term trazodone benefit dissipated after two weeks (p. 661).

Source: Hazzard’s Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8e, pp. 661.

q: A patient with Parkinson disease develops motor worsening after starting metoclopramide. Which mechanism-and-risk pairing explains the Beers recommendation to avoid it?
o: Dopamine-receptor blockade with a risk of worsening parkinsonian symptoms
Dopamine-receptor activation with a risk of worsening parkinsonian symptoms
Dopamine-receptor blockade with an expected improvement in parkinsonian symptoms
Dopamine-receptor activation with an expected improvement in parkinsonian symptoms
explanation:
**Dopamine-receptor antagonism** is the relevant mechanism. The Parkinson disease criterion lists metoclopramide among drugs to avoid because they are "Dopamine-receptor antagonists with the potential to worsen parkinsonian symptoms" (p. 2067).

**A. Dopamine-receptor blockade with a risk of worsening parkinsonian symptoms.** Correct, This matches both the mechanism and the adverse motor effect identified in the criterion (p. 2067).
**B. Dopamine-receptor activation with a risk of worsening parkinsonian symptoms.** Wrong, Metoclopramide is listed as an antagonist, not a dopamine-receptor activator (p. 2067).
**C. Dopamine-receptor blockade with an expected improvement in parkinsonian symptoms.** Wrong, Although blockade is the listed mechanism, the expected risk is worsening rather than improvement (p. 2067).
**D. Dopamine-receptor activation with an expected improvement in parkinsonian symptoms.** Wrong, Both the receptor action and direction of motor effect conflict with the criterion (p. 2067).

Source: AGS Beers 2023, pp. 2067.
ref: Hazzard Ch 61 — PARKINSON DISEASE AND RELATED DISORDERS · Harrison Ch 433 — Approach to the Patient with Neurologic Disease

q: גבר בן 84 עם heart failure (EF 35%) ו-CKD stage 4 (eGFR 22) מגיע לקליניקה. אשתו מדווחת שהוא מבולבל יותר בימים האחרונים וישן במהלך היום. התרופות כוללות furosemide 80mg BID, spironolactone 25mg daily, metoprolol 50mg BID, ו-gabapentin 300mg TID לנוירופתיה. תוצאות מעבדה: K+ 5.8, Na+ 134, BUN 78, Cr 3.2. איזו התאמה תרופתית היא המתאימה ביותר?
o: הפסקת spironolactone
הפחתת gabapentin ל-300mg daily
החלפת furosemide ב-bumetanide
הפחתת metoprolol ל-25mg BID
explanation:
התשובה הנכונה היא הפחתת gabapentin ל-300mg daily. עם eGFR של 22, gabapentin מחייב הפחתת מינון משמעותית (מקסימום 300mg daily ב-CKD stage 4). הצטברות gabapentin גורמת ל-sedation, delirium ושיבוש מחזור שינה-ערות — מה שמסביר את הסימפטומים של המטופל.

אופציה א' (הפסקת spironolactone) היא ה-trap answer. למרות שהיפרקלמיה מצביעה על צורך בהפחתת spironolactone, היא אינה מסבירה את הסימפטומים הנוירולוגיים. קלינאים רבים מתמקדים בערך המעבדה החריג במקום לקשר את הסימפטומים לרעילות תרופתית.

אופציה ג' (החלפת משתנים) אינה מטפלת בתלונה המרכזית של delirium וישנוניות יממית, אף שרוטציה של loop diuretics יכולה לסייע בהתנגדות למשתנים.

אופציה ד' (הפחתת metoprolol) עלולה להחמיר את שליטת ה-heart failure מבלי לטפל בגורם הסביר לסימפטומים.

Clinical Pearl: Gabapentin ו-pregabalin מחייבים הפחתת מינון אגרסיבית ב-CKD — 50% מינון ב-CKD3, 25% ב-CKD4, ו-10-15% ב-CKD5. הצטברות מתבטאת כ-'gabapentin encephalopathy' עם delirium, somnolence ומיוקלונוס. יש לחשב מחדש מינונים בכל שינוי בתפקוד הכליות.
ref: Hazzard Ch 22 — MEDICATION PRESCRIBING AND DE-PRESCRIBING
retiredReason: Two defensible answers by Hazzard pp. 1181-1182; a look-alike question teaches the opposite.

q: A 91-year-old woman with moderate dementia has increasing agitation and refuses medication. She has round-the-clock caregivers, an MMSE score of 14/30, and needs assistance with all activities of daily living. Her family requests risperidone. Her daughter, the healthcare proxy, says, "We want her comfortable without hastening her death." Which approach follows the 2023 AGS Beers Criteria?
o: Begin risperidone before behavioral approaches, relying on continuous supervision for safety.
Discuss stroke and mortality risks and assess nonpharmacologic approaches before prescribing.
Substitute scheduled lorazepam before behavioral approaches, relying on its cognitive safety.
Begin risperidone without a risk discussion, relying on comfort as sufficient justification.
explanation:
**Antipsychotics in dementia** are associated with "Increased risk of stroke and greater rate of cognitive decline and mortality in persons with dementia" (p. 2059). Beers advises avoiding them for behavioral problems unless specified conditions involving nonpharmacologic treatment failure or substantial harm are met (p. 2066). The stated presentation does not establish those conditions; discussing risks and nonpharmacologic options therefore follows the criteria.

**A. Begin risperidone before behavioral approaches, relying on continuous supervision for safety.** Wrong, continuous supervision does not replace the criteria concerning nonpharmacologic options and substantial harm (p. 2066).
**B. Discuss stroke and mortality risks and assess nonpharmacologic approaches before prescribing.** Correct, this addresses the stated risks and the conditions for considering an antipsychotic for dementia-related behavior (pp. 2059, 2066).
**C. Substitute scheduled lorazepam before behavioral approaches, relying on its cognitive safety.** Wrong, benzodiazepines also carry adverse CNS effects in dementia; substituting one does not establish a cognitively safe approach (p. 2066).
**D. Begin risperidone without a risk discussion, relying on comfort as sufficient justification.** Wrong, a comfort goal does not remove the documented stroke, cognitive, and mortality risks or the prescribing conditions (pp. 2059, 2066).

Source: AGS Beers Criteria 2023, pp. 2059, 2066.
label: Source: AGS Beers 2023 · pp.2059, 2066, Tables 2–3

q: An 82-year-old man develops hyponatremia after starting sertraline. Sodium is 124 mEq/L, serum osmolality is low, and the urine is concentrated. He is euvolemic without edema, orthostasis, or signs of heart failure. Renal function is stable, and thyroid and adrenal function are normal. Which mechanism best fits?
o: Hypervolemic hyponatremia due to heart failure
Euvolemic hyponatremia due to drug-associated SIADH
Hypovolemic hyponatremia due to fluid losses
Hypervolemic hyponatremia due to nephrotic syndrome
explanation:
**Volume status** guides the differential diagnosis of hyponatremia. Hazzard places medication-associated SIADH and SSRIs in the euvolemic category; concentrated urine reflects impaired excretion of excess water (p. 587).
"The vast majority of cases of hyponatremia are associated with an inappropriately high urine osmolality, that is, an inability to excrete a free water load." (p. 587).

**A. Hypervolemic hyponatremia due to heart failure.** Wrong, heart failure belongs to the hypervolemic category, whereas the stem specifies euvolemia without heart-failure signs (p. 587).
**B. Euvolemic hyponatremia due to drug-associated SIADH.** Correct, the medication exposure, euvolemia, and concentrated urine fit the source category; this is a clinical inference, not proof of drug causation (p. 587).
**C. Hypovolemic hyponatremia due to fluid losses.** Wrong, the stem lacks the hypovolemic findings described in the source, such as orthostatic hypotension (p. 587).
**D. Hypervolemic hyponatremia due to nephrotic syndrome.** Wrong, nephrotic syndrome is in the hypervolemic category and does not match the stated volume status (p. 587).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 587.
ref: Hazzard Ch 22 — MEDICATION PRESCRIBING AND DE-PRESCRIBING

q: A 76-year-old woman with diabetes and hypertension is brought by her daughter because she leaves the stove on and forgets medications. MMSE is 24/30 with memory and orientation deficits. HbA1c is 9.2%. She takes metformin 1000 mg twice daily, glyburide 10 mg twice daily, and lisinopril 20 mg daily. BP is 142/84 and Cockcroft–Gault creatinine clearance is 48 mL/min. Which paired approach best reflects Hazzard’s concerns about drug choice and treatment intensity?
o: Retain glyburide for its short half-life; consider less intensive glycemic targets
Avoid glyburide for its hypoglycemia risk; intensify treatment because of cognitive impairment
Avoid glyburide for its hypoglycemia risk; consider less intensive glycemic targets
Retain glyburide for its short half-life; intensify treatment because of cognitive impairment
explanation:
**Hypoglycemia risk and self-management capacity** must inform treatment planning (pp. 1568–1569, 1579). Hazzard states that glyburide is associated with higher hypoglycemia risk because of its long half-life and "is not recommended in this population" (p. 1579). Cognitive impairment can interfere with complex treatment tasks and may preclude an intensive program (pp. 1568–1569); this supports reassessing the target and regimen, not ignoring her hyperglycemia.

**A. Retain glyburide for its short half-life; consider less intensive glycemic targets.** Wrong, a less intensive target merits consideration, but glyburide has a long half-life and higher hypoglycemia risk in older people (pp. 1569, 1579).
**B. Avoid glyburide for its hypoglycemia risk; intensify treatment because of cognitive impairment.** Wrong, avoiding glyburide fits the drug warning, but cognitive impairment is a reason to reassess feasibility and safety rather than itself a reason to intensify treatment (pp. 1568–1569, 1579).
**C. Avoid glyburide for its hypoglycemia risk; consider less intensive glycemic targets.** Correct, both avoiding the flagged drug and reconsidering treatment intensity address concerns documented in the source (pp. 1568–1569, 1579).
**D. Retain glyburide for its short half-life; intensify treatment because of cognitive impairment.** Wrong, both rationales conflict with the source: glyburide has a long half-life, and cognitive impairment can make intensive treatment unsuitable (pp. 1569, 1579).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 1579, 1569, 1568.

q: An 88-year-old man is found after lying for a prolonged period in a cold environment. His core temperature is 30°C, with a pulse and spontaneous breathing. After initial stabilization, which approach to hypothermia is supported by Hazzard?
o: Passive rewarming in a warm room, volume replacement, and ECG monitoring
External rewarming with an electric blanket, volume replacement, and ECG monitoring
Active rewarming of the body core, volume replacement, and ECG monitoring
External rewarming in a warm bath, volume replacement, and ECG monitoring
explanation:
**Active core rewarming** is required for the severity of hypothermia described.
